Definition: For k=1 the two alpha commutators with their adjoints vanish because they are scalar. The source equations reduce to PQ=0 and PP^dagger=Q^dagger Q; this specialization follows directly from the two displayed equations.

risk_review.notes: Checked raw map types, stable word-span and costability, zero-FI orbit set, smooth unitary framed S4 objects, anti-Hermitian charge convention q=-k, quaternionic incidence and sigma, alpha-plane orientation and positive Ward pairing. Torus commutes with sigma projectively (the conjugated diagonal differs by scalar t1*t2). Definition asserts neither existence nor integrality. Fibre inclusion square commutes; no empirical premise or proof of nature is asserted.

citations.quote:
Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. Write $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $P:W\to V$, and $Q:V\to W$. The Donaldson source convention for these four matrices is

$$[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]+PQ=0,\qquad [\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]-PP^\dagger+Q^\dagger Q=0.$$

The second equality is an equality of Hermitian endomorphisms of $V$. It is an algebraic convention from the displayed source equations; it does not by itself assert the full-rank condition on the source's ADHM linear map or an identification with the run's raw moment maps.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and equip $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with the standard Hermitian inner products $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j\overline{u_j}v_j$, which are conjugate-linear in the first variable. For a linear map $T:E\to F$ between these spaces, its Hermitian adjoint $T^\dagger:F\to E$ is characterized by $\langle Tu,v\rangle_F=\langle u,T^\dagger v\rangle_E$; in the standard bases its matrix is the conjugate transpose. For $A,B\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, define their commutator by $[A,B]:=AB-BA$. Let

$$\mathscr D_{k,N}=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W),\qquad \operatorname{Herm}(V)=\{H\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V):H^\dagger=H\}.$$

Here $\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ is regarded as a real vector space. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)\in\mathscr D_{k,N}$. The complex and real moment maps are the maps $\mu_{\mathbb C}:\mathscr D_{k,N}\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ and $\mu_{\mathbb R}:\mathscr D_{k,N}\to\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ defined by

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

derivations.claim: Componentwise conjugation of $[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]+PQ=0$ gives $[\overline{\alpha_1},\overline{\alpha_2}]+\overline P\,\overline Q=0$. By [F2], this is exactly $\mu_{\mathbb C}(B,I,J)=0$.

Since $(\overline{\alpha_i})^\dagger=\overline{\alpha_i^\dagger}$, the commutator part of $\mu_{\mathbb R}$ is $\overline C$. Also $II^\dagger=\overline X$ and $J^\dagger J=\overline Y$. Thus $\mu_{\mathbb R}=\overline C+\overline X-\overline Y$. Conjugating the source real equation gives $\overline C-\overline X+\overline Y=0$, so the raw expression on such a source solution is $2(\overline X-\overline Y)=2\overline C$.

To verify that the source equations permit $C\ne0$, take $k=N=2$, $\alpha_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\alpha_2=0$, $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $Q=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. Then $[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]+PQ=0$, $C=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, $X=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$, and $Y=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$, so $C-X+Y=0$. Under the proposed substitution the raw real moment map is $\operatorname{diag}(2,-2)\ne0$. This checks the claimed failure using only the source algebraic equations; it makes no claim that this tuple satisfies the separate source full-rank condition.

boundaries.evidence: At k=0 every endomorphism of V=0 is zero, so conjugation gives mu_C=mu_R=2 bar C=0. The theorem's counterexample to the general implication remains its explicit k=N=2 tuple, not this vacuous specialization.

Proof 2.1 computes mu_R=2 bar C on source solutions. Therefore C=0 makes the raw real moment vanish, while Proof 3.1 gives C=diag(1,-1), alpha_2=0 and PQ=0, yielding the explicit nonzero raw value diag(2,-2).

For k=1 each alpha_i is scalar, hence C=0. The source real equation forces X=Y and Proof 2.1 gives mu_R=0 in that special case; the claimed general failure is witnessed at k=N=2 rather than asserted for scalar k.

Proof 3.1 intentionally uses rank-deficient P=diag(1,0), Q=diag(0,1), with alpha_2=0. Its final sentence disclaims the separate full-rank condition, so the counterexample proves failure from the source algebraic equations alone.

boundaries.reason: The substitution and two moment equations contain no FI parameter or deformation interval. Proof 3.1 is a fixed 2-by-2 algebraic counterexample, with no chamber limit claimed.
Proof 3.1 writes all four 2-by-2 matrices explicitly; entrywise conjugation and multiplication involve no selection of orbit representatives or an arbitrary indexed family.

boundaries.evidence: Proof 2.1 yields mu_R=2 bar C on source solutions. If the substituted raw real moment vanishes, division by the nonzero real scalar 2 and conjugation imply C=0; thus the obstruction vanishes only at C=0.

Statement: For a source solution with C=0, the same formula mu_R=2 bar C gives mu_R=0. This local algebraic equivalence concerns that substitution only and does not establish a source-to-regular-ADHM correspondence.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a nonempty, connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. Let $G\subseteq U(V,h)$ be a compact non-Abelian matrix Lie group in its specified global form, let $\pi:P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle in a specified bundle sector (an isomorphism class of smooth principal bundles under isomorphisms over $X$), and let $\omega$ be a supplied smooth principal connection. Let $B:\mathfrak g\times\mathfrak g\to\mathbb R$ be a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form invariant under $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$. For local sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$. If $F_i=\sum_a e_a F_i^a$ in a finite basis of $\mathfrak g$, define $B(F_i\wedge F_i):=\sum_{a,b}B(e_a,e_b)F_i^a\wedge F_i^b$; this expression is independent of the basis. Invariance of $B$ makes the local expressions $\beta_B|_{U_i}:=(8\pi^2)^{-1}B(F_i\wedge F_i)$ restrictions of a global four-form $\beta_B$. The **trace-normalized topological charge** is

$$
q_B(P,\omega):=\int_X\beta_B.
$$

The number $q_B(P,\omega)$ is independent of the supplied connection. For a general compact matrix group and invariant $B$, it is a real characteristic number; no integrality is asserted. In the special case $G=SU(2)$ in its defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$, with $h(v,w)=w^*v$ (linear in $v$ and conjugate-linear in $w$) and $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$, the associated Hermitian bundle $E=P\times_{SU(2)}\mathbb C^2$ has

$$
q_B(P,\omega)=-\langle c_2(E),[X]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,
$$

where $c_2(E)\in H^4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the integral second Chern class and $[X]\in H_4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the orientation fundamental class. This sign is fixed by the library convention $c(E,\nabla)=\det(I-\Omega_\nabla/(2\pi i))$.

The Hodge operator $*_g$ on two-forms is characterized by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$ and acts componentwise on $\mathfrak g$-valued forms. Set $F_i^+=(F_i+*_gF_i)/2$ and $F_i^-=(F_i-*_gF_i)/2$. The self-dual sector consists of connections with $F_i^-=0$, equivalently $F_i=*_gF_i$; the anti-self-dual (ASD) sector consists of connections with $F_i^+=0$, equivalently $F_i=-*_gF_i$. These conditions are independent of the local section.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle with a principal connection form $\omega$ associated to $H$, using $Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_0p\exp_G(tZ)$ for the right action. For Lie-algebra-valued forms use the graded bracket defined by alternating shuffle and the Lie bracket; in degree one, $[A\wedge B](X,Y)=[A(X),B(Y)]-[A(Y),B(X)]$. Define

$$\Omega_\omega:=d\omega+\frac12[\omega\wedge\omega],\qquad D_\omega\eta:=d\eta+[\omega\wedge\eta].$$

Then $\Omega_\omega$ is horizontal and $\operatorname{Ad}$-equivariant, and $\Omega_\omega=\omega\circ K_H$ for the imported vertical-valued curvature $K_H(X,Y)=-v([hX,hY])$. For any trivializing cover with smooth sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=s_i^*\Omega_\omega$. On an overlap, let $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to G$ be the smooth map determined by $s_j=s_i g_{ij}$, and write $\theta_L(g_{ij})=g_{ij}^*\theta_L$ for the left Maurer–Cartan form. Then

$$A_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}A_i+\theta_L(g_{ij}),\qquad F_i=dA_i+\frac12[A_i\wedge A_i],\qquad F_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}F_i,\qquad D_{A_i}F_i=0,$$

where $D_{A_i}\eta:=d\eta+[A_i\wedge\eta]$. The transition equations concern changes of local sections; they do not identify an arbitrary map $M\to G$ with a global automorphism of a nontrivial bundle.
Assume countable choice. For $n\ge1$, $H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(S^n)$ is $\mathbb R$ in degrees $0,n$ and zero otherwise. For $S^0$ it is $\mathbb R^2$ in degree zero and zero otherwise.
For every natural number $n\ge2$, the unit sphere $S^n\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ is simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]).

A connection on a finite-rank smooth vector bundle $E\to M$ is flat if and
only if every point of $M$ has a neighborhood carrying a local frame
$(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ of parallel sections, meaning $\nabla_Xe_a=0$ for every
local vector field $X$ and every $a$.

Let $E\to M$ carry a flat connection, meaning $R^\nabla=0$. For every
$p\in M$ there is a coordinate ball $U$ about $p$ such that, whenever two
piecewise smooth paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to U$ have the same initial
and terminal points,

$$P_{\gamma_0}=P_{\gamma_1}.$$

This is a local assertion; it makes no claim about transport around loops in a
non-simply-connected larger domain.

Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold,
possibly with boundary. If $E\to M$ is a rank-$r$ complex vector bundle with
complex connection $\nabla$ and curvature $\Omega$, define the total Chern form
$$c(\nabla)=\det\!\left(I-\frac{\Omega}{2\pi i}\right)=\sum_{j=0}^r c_j(\nabla),$$
where $c_j(\nabla)$ has degree $2j$. For a Hermitian connection these forms
are real-valued; a general complex connection need not give real-valued forms.

For a rank-$r$ real vector bundle with real connection $\nabla$, let
$E_{\mathbb C}=E\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ carry the complexified
connection $\nabla_{\mathbb C}$ and set
$$p_j(\nabla)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})\quad\text{in degree }4j,\qquad p(\nabla)=\sum_{j\geq0}p_j(\nabla).$$
Then $p_0=1$, $p_j=0$ when $2j>r$, and every $p_j(\nabla)$ is real-valued,
even if $\nabla$ is not metric-compatible. If $\nabla$ is compatible with a
Euclidean metric, each odd Chern form $c_{2j+1}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})$ vanishes
pointwise. Assume full Axiom of Choice (AC); for every real connection each
$c_{2j+1}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})$ is then exact, with AC used through existence
of a metric-compatible connection and the transgression lemma.

If $E$ is an oriented Euclidean bundle of even rank $2m$ and $\nabla$ is
metric-compatible, define
$$e(\nabla)=\operatorname{Pf}\!\left(\frac{\Omega}{2\pi}\right),$$
where the Pfaffian uses the ordered oriented orthonormal frame and
$\operatorname{Pf}\!\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&a\\-a&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)=a$.
These curvature evaluations are closed forms. In rank zero,
$c(\nabla)=p(\nabla)=e(\nabla)=1$. The Euler form is defined here only for
oriented even-rank Euclidean bundles with a metric-compatible connection.

Assume AC. Let $E\to B$ be a numerable complex rank-$n$ bundle with $n\geq1$
over a path-connected CW complex $B$ (or over one of the CW-type bases of
[[thm-integral-complex-projective-bundle-theorem]]). By that theorem there are
unique classes $a_i\in H^{2i}(B;\mathbb Z)$, $1\leq i\leq n$, such that
$$x_E^{\,n}-a_1x_E^{\,n-1}+a_2x_E^{\,n-2}-\cdots+(-1)^na_n=0\qquad\text{in }H^{2n}(P(E);\mathbb Z),$$
where $x_E\in H^2(P(E);\mathbb Z)$ is the Euler class of the underlying real
bundle of the tautological line
([[def-complex-projective-bundle-and-tautological-complex-line]]). The
**Chern classes** of $E$ are these coefficients:
$$c_i(E):=a_i\in H^{2i}(B;\mathbb Z)\qquad(1\leq i\leq n),$$
completed by the conventions $c_0(E):=1\in H^0(B;\mathbb Z)$ and
$c_i(E):=0$ for $i>n$, and the **total Chern class** is the finite sum
$c(E):=\sum_{i\geq0}c_i(E)=1+c_1(E)+\cdots+c_n(E)\in H^*(B;\mathbb Z)$.

For the zero bundle of rank $0$ the conventions give $c(0_B)=1$. The definition
depends only on the isomorphism class of $E$, because an isomorphism of
bundles induces an isomorphism of projective bundles pulling $x$ back to $x$
and hence preserves the unique relation. For a complex line bundle $L\to B$ one
has $P(L)\cong B$ over $B$ with $\gamma_L$ corresponding to $L$ under that
identification, so the relation is $x_L-c_1(L)=0$; since $x_L=e(L_{\mathbb R})$
under the identification, this gives
$$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R}).$$
This is the normalization used throughout the page: the first Chern class of a
complex line is the Euler class of its underlying real bundle in the complex
orientation, not a separately chosen normalization.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff
second-countable smooth manifold, possibly with boundary or empty, and let
$\rho_M:H^*(M;\mathbb Z)\to H^*(M;\mathbb R)$ be induced by
$\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$. Write $J_M$ for the natural de Rham
isomorphism from real de Rham cohomology to singular cohomology with real
coefficients.

For every finite-rank smooth complex bundle $E\to M$ with a Hermitian metric
and Hermitian connection $\nabla$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([c_j(\nabla)])=\rho_M(c_j(E)).$$
For every finite-rank smooth real bundle $V\to M$ with any real connection
$D$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([p_j(D)])=\rho_M(p_j(V)).$$
For every oriented Euclidean bundle $W\to M$ of even rank with a
metric-compatible connection $\nabla$, and its Thom-normalized Euler class,
$$J_M([e(\nabla)])=\rho_M(e(W)).$$
Here $c_j(\nabla)$, $p_j(D)$, and $e(\nabla)$ use the normalizations in
[[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], while $c_j(E)$,
$p_j(V)$, and $e(W)$ are the published topological classes. In particular
$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line and
$p_j(V)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(V_{\mathbb C})$. These are equalities after passage to
real coefficients; no equality with integral torsion is asserted.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$, possibly with boundary, integration on smooth simplices followed by the inverse of restriction from continuous to smooth singular cohomology gives a natural isomorphism of unital graded real algebras
$$J_M:H^*_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^*_{\mathrm{sing}}(M;\mathbb R).$$
The source product is wedge of form classes, the target product is the front/back singular cup product, and both stars denote direct sums of the homogeneous groups. Naturality is for smooth maps. No compactness assumption is imposed.

derivations.claim: In a local unitary frame let $F_{\det A}$ be the curvature of the induced connection on $\det E$. The induced connection on the top exterior power has local connection matrix $\operatorname{tr}A$, hence $F_{\det A}=\operatorname{tr}F_A$. Put $\eta=-i\operatorname{tr}F_A$, a real two-form because $F_A$ is anti-Hermitian. By [F2], $d\eta=0$, and the linearity of trace in $F_A^+=0$ gives $*_g\eta=-\eta$.

By [A1] and [F3], $\eta$ is exact, so choose a smooth real one-form $\alpha$ with $\eta=d\alpha$. The ASD equation gives $\int_{S^4}\eta\wedge *_g\eta=-\int_{S^4}d\alpha\wedge\eta=-\int_{S^4}d(\alpha\wedge\eta)=0$, since $d\eta=0$ and $S^4$ is compact without boundary. The integrand $\eta\wedge *_g\eta$ is the nonnegative squared norm density of the real form $\eta$; zero integral forces $\eta=0$ pointwise. Hence $F_{\det A}=0$ and the determinant connection is flat.

Choose the unit vector $v_\infty$ in $(\det E)_\infty$ specified by the determinant of the framing. For any $x\in S^4$, parallel transport $v_\infty$ along a piecewise smooth path from $\infty$ to $x$. If two paths are chosen, their concatenation is a loop. By [F3] the loop is null-homotopic; subdivide a null-homotopy square into finitely many rectangles mapped into coordinate balls, which is possible by compactness and a Lebesgue number for the pulled-back coordinate-ball cover. On each rectangle [F4] makes boundary transport the identity. Multiplying around the subdivision cancels the interior edges, so the two path transports agree. The resulting section is smooth by local parallel frames, is parallel by construction, and agrees with $v_\infty$; uniqueness follows from uniqueness of parallel sections along each path. Its unit norm is preserved by unitary parallel transport, so the determinant framing reduces the structure group to $SU(N)$.

Writing $C=-F_A/(2\pi i)$, the degree-four term of $\det(I+C)$ is $c_2(A)=\tfrac12((\operatorname{tr}C)\wedge(\operatorname{tr}C)-\operatorname{tr}(C\wedge C))$. Step 2.1 gives $\operatorname{tr}F_A=0$, so this reduces to $c_2(A)=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$. Therefore $q_N=-\int_{S^4}c_2(A)$. By [F5] and the de Rham integration pairing, $\int_{S^4}c_2(A)=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$, an integer. Finally $q_N=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int B(F_A\wedge F_A)$ for the positive invariant form $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_N(XY)$; since $F_A=-*_gF_A$ and $B$ is positive definite, $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int B(F_A\wedge *_gF_A)\leq0$. This proves the stated sign and nonnegativity of $k=-q_N$.

boundaries.reason: The input is a supplied rank N>=2 bundle over S4, and the integration in Proof 2.1 is over that fixed nonempty compact sphere. There is no empty index family or rank-zero extension in the determinant reduction assertion.

boundaries.evidence: Proof 2.1 proves tr F_A=0 by exactness and its zero norm integral. Proof 4.1 gives q_N=-(8pi^2)^-1 integral |F_A|_B^2; for q_N=0 the same nonnegative continuous-integrand argument forces F_A=0, while zero determinant curvature holds for every stated ASD input.
The Statement excludes rank N=1 by N>=2. Charge k=1 is not excluded: Proof 4.1 gives q_N=-1 whenever the supplied bundle has c_2[S4]=1, without asserting a connection exists in that sector.

citations.quote:
Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

derivations.claim:
Pair $(
abla^*
abla+cI)s=0$ with $s$ using the Hermitian metric and integrate over the compact boundaryless $S^4$ in [F1]. By [F2], the result is $0=\int_{S^4}|
abla s|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}+c\int_{S^4}|s|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}$. Both terms are nonnegative and $c>0$, so $\int_{S^4}|s|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}=0$.

The pointwise function $|s|^2$ is continuous and nonnegative. If it were positive at some point, it would be bounded below by a positive constant on a nonempty open neighborhood, which has positive Riemannian volume, contradicting the zero integral in step 1.1. Therefore $s=0$ everywhere.

boundaries.evidence: Statement: The empty or zero-dimensional case is included and checked. the proof.

The section s=0 satisfies the equation, and Proof 1.1–2.1 proves it is the only smooth solution. The coefficient c=0 is excluded by c>0: at c=0 parallel sections can remain in the kernel and the coercive term used in Proof 1.1 disappears.
At c=1, Proof 1.1 reads 0=integral |nabla s|^2+integral |s|^2 and still forces s=0. The same reasoning applies to a rank-one Hermitian bundle, since no rank>=2 condition is imposed.

For a rank-zero bundle the only section is zero, so the conclusion is vacuous. A degenerate Hermitian form is not allowed; positivity of the specified metric and c>0 are exactly what make the two integrals nonnegative in Proof 1.1.

The coefficient range c>0 excludes c=0, and Proof 1.1 uses strict positivity rather than a limiting argument. S4 has no boundary, so the formal-adjoint identity has no boundary contribution or unmentioned boundary condition.

boundaries.reason: The bundle, connection and section are given. Proof 1.1 integrates their norms, and Proof 2.1 argues from a single hypothetical positive point; it selects no family of sections or frames.

boundaries.evidence: The stated implication is the nontrivial direction: if (nabla* nabla+cI)s=0, Proof 1.1 gives integral |s|^2=0 and Proof 2.1 gives s=0 by continuity and positive volume.

The zero section is annihilated by both the linear covariant Laplacian and cI, so s=0 satisfies the displayed equation. Together with Proof 1.1–2.1 this identifies the smooth kernel as {0}, without a claim at c=0.

citations.quote:
Let $n\in\{2,3\}$, $X=\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$, $X^{an}$ its complex analytic space, and $\eta:X^{an}\to X$ the canonical morphism of ringed spaces. Let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ denote the abelian category of all sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules on a ringed space $Y$, and let $D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y))$ be the category of bounded-below cochain complexes in it with quasi-isomorphisms inverted; use the cochain shift convention $K[q]^m=K^{m+q}$ with differential $(-1)^q d_K$. For coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ placed in degree zero, define the global derived morphism groups

$$\operatorname{Ext}^q_Y(\mathcal F,\mathcal G):=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y))}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G[q]),\qquad q\ge0.$$

On $X$, these groups can be computed from a bounded cochain complex $P^\bullet$ of finite-rank locally free sheaves together with a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to\mathcal F$, by $H^q(R\Gamma(X,\mathcal H om^\bullet(P^\bullet,\mathcal G)))$; the analogous computation applies to the analytified resolution on $X^{an}$.

Define analytification by $\operatorname{An}_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F^{an}:=\eta^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{\eta^{-1}\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_{X^{an}}$. It is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence from coherent algebraic $\mathcal O_X$-modules (locally finitely presented modules) to coherent analytic $\mathcal O_{X^{an}}$-modules (locally finitely presented modules). For every coherent $\mathcal F$, the canonical cohomology comparison

$$\gamma^q_{\mathcal F}:H^q(X,\mathcal F)=R^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q(X^{an},\mathcal F^{an})=R^q\Gamma(X^{an},\mathcal F^{an})$$

is an isomorphism for all $q\ge0$. For coherent $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$, the map

$$\epsilon^q_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}:\operatorname{Ext}^q_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}^q_{X^{an}}(\mathcal F^{an},\mathcal G^{an})$$

is the map obtained by analytifying a finite locally free resolution of $\mathcal F$ and applying the cohomology comparisons term by term; independence of the chosen resolution makes it canonical. It is an isomorphism for all $q\ge0$, and for $q=0$ it is the usual comparison of algebraic and holomorphic morphisms. Here $H^q$ is sheaf cohomology computed by right-derived global sections using a supplied functorial injective-resolution datum.

Let $i:L_\infty\hookrightarrow X$ be the fixed hyperplane inclusion, where $L_\infty=\{z_0=0\}$, and let $i^{an}:L_\infty^{an}\hookrightarrow X^{an}$ be its analytification. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module, $i^*\mathcal F:=\mathcal O_{L_\infty}\otimes_{i^{-1}\mathcal O_X}i^{-1}\mathcal F$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $(i^*\mathcal F)^{an}\cong(i^{an})^*(\mathcal F^{an})$, so restriction to the fixed hyperplane commutes with analytification.

For the family clause, let $S$ be a finite-type complex scheme, put $Y=X\times S$, and let $p:Y\to S$ be projection. Write $\eta_S:S^{an}\to S$ and $\eta_Y:Y^{an}\to Y$ for analytification; then $Y^{an}\cong X^{an}\times S^{an}$, with analytic projection $p^{an}:Y^{an}\to S^{an}$. Let $\mathcal E$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module flat over $S$, meaning that for every $y\in Y$ the stalk $\mathcal E_y$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,p(y)}$. For each closed point $s\in S$ with residue field $\kappa(s)=\mathbb C$, let $j_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ be its inclusion, $X_s:=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, $i_s:X_s\hookrightarrow Y$, $p_s:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ the projection, and $\mathcal E_s:=i_s^*\mathcal E$. Let $t\in S^{an}$ be the corresponding analytic point, with inclusion $j_t:\{t\}\to S^{an}$, fiber $X_t^{an}:=Y^{an}\times_{S^{an}}\{t\}$, inclusion $i_t^{an}:X_t^{an}\hookrightarrow Y^{an}$, projection $p_t^{an}:X_t^{an}\to\{t\}$, and $\mathcal E_t^{an}:=(i_t^{an})^*\mathcal E^{an}$. For a morphism $f$ of ringed spaces, write $R^qf_*$ for the $q$th cohomology sheaf of the derived direct image computed from a supplied functorial injective resolution; on an open $V$ of the target, $(f_*I)(V)=I(f^{-1}V)$. The canonical algebraic base-change map

$$\beta^{alg}_{q,s}:(R^qp_*\mathcal E)\otimes_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s)\longrightarrow H^q(X_s,\mathcal E_s)$$

is the cohomology-and-base-change map induced by the derived base-change morphism $Lj_s^*Rp_*\mathcal E\to R(p_s)_*Li_s^*\mathcal E$, where $L(-)^*$ is the left-derived pullback functor, after the canonical edge identification $(R^qp_*\mathcal E)\otimes\kappa(s)\cong H^q(Lj_s^*Rp_*\mathcal E)$ when the direct-image cohomology sheaves in the relevant degrees are locally free. Define $\beta^{an}_{q,t}:(R^qp^{an}_*\mathcal E^{an})\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S^{an}}}\kappa(t)\to H^q(X_t^{an},\mathcal E_t^{an})$ by the analogous analytic derived base-change morphism and edge identification. Define the canonical comparison

$$c_q:(R^qp_*\mathcal E)^{an}\longrightarrow R^qp^{an}_*\mathcal E^{an}$$

by the following construction. For every algebraic open $V\subseteq S$, the morphism $\eta_Y^{-1}\mathcal E\to\mathcal E^{an}$ and the natural pullback map on sheaf cohomology give a map $H^q(p^{-1}V,\mathcal E)\to H^q((p^{an})^{-1}(\eta_S^{-1}V),\mathcal E^{an})$. These maps are compatible with restriction, so they induce a morphism from the sheafification of the first cohomology presheaf, identified with $R^qp_*\mathcal E$, to $\eta_{S*}R^qp^{an}_*\mathcal E^{an}$. The adjoint of this morphism under $\eta_S^{-1}(-)\otimes_{\eta_S^{-1}\mathcal O_S}\mathcal O_{S^{an}}\dashv\eta_{S*}$ is $c_q$. Whenever the direct-image cohomology sheaves are locally free of finite rank and both base-change maps $\beta^{alg}_{q,s}$ and $\beta^{an}_{q,t}$ are isomorphisms for every such $s$ and its corresponding $t$, $c_q$ is an isomorphism; on each fiber its induced map commutes with the two base-change maps and the absolute cohomology comparison $\gamma^q_{\mathcal E_s}$. No assertion is made that an arbitrary holomorphic family over a nonproper algebraic base algebraizes.

For every $r$-subset $I$ of a basis of an $n$-dimensional $V$, the locus $p_I\ne0$ in $\operatorname{Gr}(r,V)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf A_k^{r(n-r)}$; these loci cover the Grassmannian and have regular transition maps.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the relative Proj construction
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-relative-proj-quasi-coherent-graded-algebra]]).
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $E$ be a finite locally free
$\mathcal O_S$-module of locally constant rank $r\ge0$
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]). Write
$$\operatorname{Sym}(E)=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\operatorname{Sym}^d(E)$$
for the symmetric algebra of $E$
([[def-symmetric-algebra-qc-module]]): a quasi-coherent graded
$\mathcal O_S$-algebra ([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]) with $\operatorname{Sym}^0(E)=\mathcal O_S$,
$\operatorname{Sym}^1(E)=E$, generated as an $\mathcal O_S$-algebra by its
degree-one part $E$, and compatible with base change $S'\to S$
([[lem-symmetric-algebra-qc-and-base-change]]).

**Definition.** The **projective bundle** of $E$ over $S$ is the relative Proj
$$\pi:\mathbb P_S(E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S\operatorname{Sym}(E)\longrightarrow S,$$
with the relative twists $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(n)$, $n\in\mathbb Z$
([[def-relative-proj-quasi-coherent-graded-algebra]]). Since
$\operatorname{Sym}(E)$ is generated in degree one, the degree-one part
$\operatorname{Sym}^1(E)=E$ generates the whole algebra, and there is a
canonical surjection
$$\pi^*E\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(1),$$
the **tautological quotient** of the pullback of $E$; it is locally given by
the coordinate sections of a projective space, over an open set on which
$E\cong\mathcal O_S^{\,r}$.

**Quotient convention.** This is the quotient (Grothendieck) convention: over
an $S$-scheme $g:T\to S$, an $S$-morphism $T\to\mathbb P_S(E)$ is the same as
an isomorphism class of surjections $g^*E\to L$ with $L$ invertible on $T$,
and the universal such quotient is the tautological quotient above; the
representing property is proved as [[thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients]].
The associated affine construction is
$\mathbb V(E)=\operatorname{Spec}_S\operatorname{Sym}(E)$; the rank-zero
case below displays its difference from $\mathbb P_S(E)$ over nonempty $S$.

**Rank zero.** If $E=0$ then $\operatorname{Sym}(E)=\mathcal O_S$ is
concentrated in degree $0$, its irrelevant ideal is $0$, and
$$\mathbb P_S(0)=\varnothing:$$
the total space is empty. This is consistent with the quotient convention,
because a surjection $0\to L$ onto an invertible sheaf exists only over the
empty scheme; the affine bundle $\mathbb V(0)=S$ is nonempty whenever $S$ is.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the relative Proj and sheaf
constructions ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $S$ be a scheme, let $E$ be a
finite locally free $\mathcal O_S$-module of locally constant rank
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]), and let
$$\pi:\mathbb P_S(E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S\operatorname{Sym}(E)\longrightarrow S$$
be its projective bundle in the quotient convention, with twist
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(1)$ and tautological quotient
$\pi^*E\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(1)$
([[def-projective-bundle-scheme]],
[[def-relative-proj-quasi-coherent-graded-algebra]]).

Then for every $S$-scheme $g:T\to S$ the assignment
$$h\longmapsto\Bigl(h^*\bigl(\pi^*E\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(1)\bigr)\Bigr)$$
is a natural bijection between

1. the set of $S$-morphisms $h:T\to\mathbb P_S(E)$, and
2. the set of isomorphism classes of surjections $g^*E\to L$ with $L$ an
   invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module ([[def-invertible-sheaf]]), where an
   isomorphism between $g^*E\to L$ and $g^*E\to L'$ is an isomorphism
   $L\to L'$ of $\mathcal O_T$-modules making the triangle commute.

Naturality means compatibility with morphisms $T'\to T$ of $S$-schemes. For
$T=\mathbb P_S(E)$ and $h=\operatorname{id}$ the class on the right is the
tautological quotient itself: $\operatorname{id}^*(\pi^*E\to\mathcal O(1))$ is
$\pi^*E\to\mathcal O(1)$. The rank-zero case is included: if $E=0$ then
$\mathbb P_S(0)=\varnothing$, and the two sides are empty for nonempty $T$ and
singletons for $T=\varnothing$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every projective morphism in the finite-dimensional
H-projective convention of this page is proper: if $f:X\to S$ factors over $S$
as
$$X\xrightarrow{i}\mathbb P^n_S\longrightarrow S$$
with $n\ge0$, $i$ a closed immersion and the second arrow the projection, then
$f$ is proper. The empty source, the empty base and the case $n=0$ are
included, and no Noetherian, field, reducedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is
imposed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]), inherited from the
Noetherian approximation and the finite-free criterion cited below. Let
$f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of finite presentation
([[def-proper-morphism]], [[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]) with
$S$ an arbitrary scheme, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal
O_X$-module ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]) that is flat over $S$
([[def-flat-and-faithfully-flat-modules-and-ring-maps]]); by [F1] $\mathcal F$
is then finitely presented.

Fix $s\in S$ and an integer $q\ge0$, write $\kappa(s)$ for the residue field
([[def-residue-field-scheme-point]]), put $X_s:=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}
\kappa(s)$ with projection $g_s:X_s\to X$ and $\mathcal F_s:=g_s^*\mathcal F$
([[def-pullback-module-ringed-spaces]]), and let
$$\varphi^q_s:(R^qf_*\mathcal F)(s)\longrightarrow H^q(X_s,\mathcal F_s)$$
be the cohomology and base-change map at $s$
([[def-base-change-map-cohomology]], [[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]]).

**(a)** If $\varphi^q_s$ is surjective, then there is an affine open
neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that for every morphism $h:T\to U$,
with $X_T:=X\times_ST$ and projection $g_T:X_T\to X$
([[def-base-change-morphism-schemes]]), the base-change map
$$h^*\bigl(R^qf_*\mathcal F|_U\bigr)\longrightarrow R^qf_{T*}(g_T^*\mathcal F)$$
of [[def-base-change-map-cohomology]] is an isomorphism of $\mathcal
O_T$-modules.

**(b)** Assume moreover that $\varphi^q_s$ is surjective. Then $R^qf_*\mathcal
F$ is locally free of finite rank in a neighbourhood of $s$
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]) if and only if $\varphi^{q-1}_s$ is
surjective; for $q=0$ the condition on $\varphi^{-1}_s$ is automatic, so
$f_*\mathcal F$ is then finite locally free near $s$.

**(c)** Under the hypothesis of (a), $\varphi^q_s$ itself is an isomorphism.

The empty source $X=\varnothing$, the zero sheaf $\mathcal F=0$, the degrees
$q=0$ and $q>0$ with $X_s=\varnothing$, and an arbitrary (not necessarily
Noetherian) base $S$ are included. No flatness or finite-presentation
hypothesis is imposed on $f$ beyond the stated ones, and no projectivity,
Noetherianness or Krull-dimension hypothesis is imposed on $S$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]), inherited from the
Noetherian approximation and the Noetherian-stage construction cited below.
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper
morphism of finite presentation ([[def-proper-morphism]],
[[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]), and let $\mathcal F$ be a
finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module
([[def-finite-type-finite-presentation-module-sheaf]]) that is flat over $A$,
meaning that for every $x\in X$ the stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is a flat module over
the local ring $A_{f(x)}=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A,f(x)}$
([[def-flat-and-faithfully-flat-modules-and-ring-maps]]).

Then there are an integer $r\ge0$ and a bounded complex $K^\bullet$ of finite
projective $A$-modules, concentrated in degrees $0,\dots,r$ and finite free in
all positive degrees, such that for every $A$-algebra $A'$ and every
$q\in\mathbb Z$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$H^q(K^\bullet\otimes_AA')\;\cong\;H^q(X_{A'},\mathcal F_{A'}),$$
where $X_{A'}:=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A'$ with
projection $p:X_{A'}\to X$ ([[def-base-change-morphism-schemes]]) and
$\mathcal F_{A'}:=p^*\mathcal F$ ([[def-pullback-module-ringed-spaces]]). The
isomorphisms are natural in the $A$-algebra $A'$ and compatible with
composition of $A$-algebra maps.

Locally on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ the complex can be made finite free: there
is an open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by affine opens $V$ such that
$K^\bullet\otimes_A\mathcal O(V)$ is a bounded complex of finite free
$\mathcal O(V)$-modules.

The empty source $X=\varnothing$, the zero sheaf $\mathcal F=0$, the
one-member case $r=0$, the zero ring $A=0$, the base change $A'=0$, the
degrees $q<0$ and $q>r$, and the case where $A$ is already finitely generated
over $\mathbb Z$ are included.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice, inherited from
the local-section formula and from Čech-to-cohomology comparison below. Let
$f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism of schemes
([[def-quasi-compact-and-quasi-separated-morphism]],
[[def-separated-morphism-schemes]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]). Then:

1. for every $q\ge0$ the higher direct image $R^qf_*\mathcal F$
   ([[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]]) is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module
   ([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]);
2. for every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$
   ([[def-affine-scheme-spectrum]]) there is a canonical isomorphism of
   $\mathcal O_V$-modules
   $$(R^qf_*\mathcal F)|_V\;\cong\;\widetilde{H^q\bigl(f^{-1}V,\mathcal F|_{f^{-1}V}\bigr)}$$
   with the associated module sheaf
   ([[def-associated-sheaf-module-affine-scheme]]) of the $A$-module
   $H^q(f^{-1}V,\mathcal F)$ ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]);
3. consequently, for every distinguished open $D(a)\subseteq V$
   ([[def-affine-scheme-spectrum]]) there is a canonical isomorphism
   $$(R^qf_*\mathcal F)(D(a))\;\cong\;H^q\bigl(f^{-1}V,\mathcal F\bigr)_a ,$$
   the localisation at $a$ of the $A$-module $H^q(f^{-1}V,\mathcal F)$
   ([[lem-associated-sheaf-sections-basic-open]]).

The empty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}0=\varnothing$, the empty scheme
$X=\varnothing$, the zero sheaf $\mathcal F=0$ and the degree $q=0$ are
included; all statements are trivial on the empty open and in degree zero they
say that $f_*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent and computed by global sections.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $I \trianglelefteq R$ satisfy $I \subseteq J(R)$, and let $M$ be a finitely generated left $R$-module. If $IM=M$, then $M=0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.

Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $X$ be a set and let $R \subseteq X \times X$ be a binary relation on $X$.
Call $R$ **entire on $X$** when

$$\text{for every } x \in X \text{ there is } y \in X \text{ with } x \mathbin{R} y .$$

The **Axiom of Dependent Choice**, written $\mathrm{DC}$, is the following
statement.

> For every nonempty set $X$, every relation $R$ entire on $X$, and every
> $a \in X$, there is a function $x : \mathbb{N} \to X$ (A function is a relation $f$ with $(a,b) \in f$ and $(a,c) \in f$ implying $b = c$; $f : A \to B$, the value $f(a)$, domain and codomain,
> The natural numbers $\mathbb{N}$ (von Neumann)) with
> $$x_0 = a \qquad \text{and} \qquad x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1} \ \text{ for every } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Here a sequence in $X$ means a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $X$, not necessarily
a real-valued sequence. As everywhere in this library $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$, and the sequence is
indexed from $0$; the term $x_0$ is the prescribed starting point $a$ and every
later term is related to its predecessor.

**What DC adds to what came before.** Choice function and
The Axiom of Choice select one element from each member of a family that is
fixed in advance, and The Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) does the same for a family indexed
by $\mathbb{N}$. In both, the family is given before any selection is made. DC is
the principle needed when the $n$-th set to select from is not known until the
first $n$ selections have been made: here the admissible values of $x_{n+1}$ are
exactly the $R$-successors of $x_n$, so the family being chosen from is built
along the choosing. Thus the displayed recursion is directly an instance of
DC; it is not itself an application of the fixed-family formulation of
countable choice. This observation concerns the input to the two axioms and
makes no claim about a nonimplication between them.

**The starting point may be dropped.** The formally weaker statement obtained by
deleting the clause $x_0 = a$ — for every nonempty $X$ and every entire $R$ there
is a sequence with $x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ for all $n$ — is an immediate
consequence of the form above, since $X$ is nonempty and any of its elements may
be taken as $a$. Conversely, assume the start-free form, and fix $X$, $R$ and $a$ as above. Let $P$ be the set of all functions $p:k\to X$ with nonzero $k\in\mathbb N$, $p(0)=a$, and $p(i)\mathbin R p(i+1)$ whenever $i+1<k$. It is a set by Separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathbb N\times X)$ (The power set $\mathcal{P}(x) = \{\, z : z \subseteq x \,\}$, The Cartesian product $A \times B := \{\, z \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(A \cup B)) : \exists a \in A\ \exists b \in B\ z = (a,b) \,\}$, The Axiom Schema of Separation: for each formula $\varphi$, $\forall \bar p\,\forall x\,\exists y\,\forall z\,(z \in y \leftrightarrow (z \in x \wedge \varphi(z,\bar p)))$); a natural is the set of its predecessors (On $\mathbb{N}$ the order is membership: $m < n \iff m \in n$). The singleton path $\{(0,a)\}$ lies in $P$.

On $P$ let $p\mathbin S q$ mean that $q$ extends $p$ by exactly one new last entry. This relation is entire: for one particular $p:k\to X$, write $k=j+1$ (Every nonzero natural number is a successor); an $R$-successor $y$ of $p(j)$ exists, and $q=p\cup\{(k,y)\}$ is the required extension. This is existential instantiation for that path, not a simultaneous choice of successors. Start-free DC now supplies a sequence $(p_n)$ with $p_n\mathbin S p_{n+1}$; its first path need not be the singleton path, but every path in $P$ already starts at $a$.

Their graphs are nested. By induction (The principle of mathematical induction), $p_n$ has at least $n+1$ entries: the initial path is nonempty, and every step adds one entry. Hence $x=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}p_n$ is a function with domain $\mathbb N$ and values in $X$. Indeed, nestedness makes all common values agree, every natural index eventually lies in a path, and no path has indices outside $\mathbb N$. Each path starts at $a$, so $x(0)=a$; for any $i$, a sufficiently long path contains both $i$ and $i+1$, giving $x(i)\mathbin R x(i+1)$. Replacement and Union form this union of the sequence of graphs. Thus the start-free and prescribed-start forms are equivalent in ZF. Every use below retains the prescribed-start convention.

**$R$ need not be an order and the terms need not be distinct.** What DC delivers
is a sequence, that is a function $\mathbb{N} \to X$, not a chain in the
order-theoretic sense (Chain in a poset). The relation may be symmetric, and the
sequence may repeat a value or be constant; all that is asserted is
$x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ at every index.

derivations.claim: Algebraize the holomorphic bundle using [A1]. Its algebraic sheaf is locally free: the holomorphic bundle is dualizable, the exact tensor equivalence transports its evaluation and coevaluation and reflects their triangle identities, and those identities give a finite dual basis on each local algebraic chart, hence a finite projective module. In a splitting C⁴=A⊕B into two-planes, a graph chart of G consists of X:A→B and the incidence is (X,[λ])↦[λ,Xλ], with p a product with P(A). In the library quotient convention it is the projective bundle of the dual of the tautological subbundle. Thus [F1] gives properness, finite presentation and flatness, and e*E is a coherent locally free sheaf flat over G.

Algebraize $\mathcal E$ by [A1], obtaining a locally free algebraic sheaf $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{alg}}$ on $Z$, and put $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{alg}}:=p_*e^*\mathcal E_{\mathrm{alg}}$. For a real line $L$, apply absolute projective GAGA to the coherent algebraic sheaf $i_*(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{alg}}|_L)$, where $i:L\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^3$ is the closed immersion. Exactness of closed-immersion direct image and the local tensor definition of analytification identify its analytic sheaf with $i^{\mathrm{an}}_*(\mathcal E|_L)$, so its cohomology is that of the trivial analytic restriction. Thus the algebraic fibre cohomology is $\mathbb C^N$ in degree zero and zero above by [F3]. The degree-one base-change map has zero target, hence is surjective. By [F2](a),(c) it is an isomorphism; the finite stalk of $R^1p_*e^*\mathcal E_{\mathrm{alg}}$ has zero residue fibre, and Nakayama kills it on a neighbourhood. The degree-one local-freeness criterion [F2](b) then gives surjectivity in degree zero. Applying [F2](a)–(c) in degree zero makes $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{alg}}$ finite locally free of rank $N$ near $L$, with degree-zero base-change isomorphisms there.

The algebraic evaluation morphism $p^*\mathcal H_{\mathrm{alg}}\to e^*\mathcal E_{\mathrm{alg}}$ is a map of rank-$N$ bundles and is invertible on $L$, since its restriction evaluates all constant sections of the trivial bundle. Its determinant-zero locus is closed. Properness of $p$ makes the image closed in the parameter neighborhood; remove that image to obtain an entire neighboring family on which evaluation is an isomorphism. This is a local neighborhood of every real line, not a claim about all complex lines.

Analytify the evaluation isomorphism from step 3.1. On every local product $V\times\mathbb P^1$, a holomorphic function is constant on each $\mathbb P^1$ fibre by the analytic degree-zero scalar assertion in [F3], and its remaining function on $V$ is holomorphic by evaluation at a fixed point. Thus $(p^{\mathrm{an}})_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr L^{\mathrm{an}}}=\mathcal O_{G^{\mathrm{an}}}$ locally. Trivializing $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{alg}}^{\mathrm{an}}$ over $V$ then gives $(p^{\mathrm{an}})_*(p^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal H_{\mathrm{alg}}^{\mathrm{an}}\cong\mathcal H_{\mathrm{alg}}^{\mathrm{an}}$. Pushing forward the analytic evaluation isomorphism therefore identifies $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{alg}}^{\mathrm{an}}$ with $\mathcal H=(p^{\mathrm{an}})_*(e^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal E$ on this neighbourhood, and identifies their evaluation morphisms. Hence the algebraic degree-zero base-change isomorphisms of step 2.1 give the analytic maps $\beta^0_{g_x}$ in the Statement. The same product calculation after any base change identifies the corresponding maps. No circular assumption of analytic base-change surjectivity or broad Grauert theorem is used.

The quaternionic involution on $G$ sends a graph $X$ to $j_BXj_A^{-1}$; its fixed graph matrices form the real four-dimensional quaternionic subspace, whose complexification is the entire graph space. These charts embed $\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ smoothly and totally really into $G$. On its incidence family evaluation is a diffeomorphism onto $Z$: the inverse sends $[v]$ to $(\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}(v,jv),[v])$, smoothly in projective charts, and $j^2=-1$ excludes dependence of $v,jv$. Restrict $\mathcal H$ to this real locus to obtain the smooth rank-$N$ bundle with the claimed fibres and evaluation. The positive pairing induces its Hermitian matrix by evaluating local section frames at a smoothly chosen point on each line; this proves smoothness and positivity, independently of parallelness. At infinity the given unitary frame induces the section-bundle frame. The only use of projective GAGA is the absolute comparison [A1]; all family base-change conclusions are established through [F2].

boundaries.evidence: The relevant family cannot be empty near a real line: every x in S4 has L_x=CP1, and Proof 2.1 computes H^0(L_x,E|L_x)=C^N with N>=2. Positive-degree fibre groups vanish; Proof 3.1 removes a closed determinant-zero image while retaining the specified line, not the entire parameter neighborhood.
Statement; steps 2.1 and 3.1: Trivial real-line restrictions have H1=0 and evaluation isomorphisms even for flat/zero-charge bundles; charge positivity is not needed.

Statement; steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1: Exact tensor descent gives locally free algebraization, while the constant H0=N and zero H1 fibre calculation rules out a section-rank jump near a real line.
