No independent converse classification is part of the claim.

risk_review.notes: Checked all five steps. Absolute GAGA algebraizes the bundle and closed-line restriction; dualizability gives local freeness. Universal incidence is the projective bundle of the dual tautological subbundle, proper, flat and finite presentation. H1=0 makes degree-one base-change surjective; the exact cited theorem and Nakayama give R1=0 then degree-zero local freeness/base change. Proper image of evaluation determinant locus is removed. Analytic product P1 functions are constant, identifying the actual analytic pushforward, without assuming Grauert surjectivity. Real graph charts and evaluation prove smooth section bundle and induced positive metric. Only absolute GAGA is used; its draft status remains explicit.

citations.quote:
Let $n\in\{2,3\}$, $X=\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$, $X^{an}$ its complex analytic space, and $\eta:X^{an}\to X$ the canonical morphism of ringed spaces. Let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ denote the abelian category of all sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules on a ringed space $Y$, and let $D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y))$ be the category of bounded-below cochain complexes in it with quasi-isomorphisms inverted; use the cochain shift convention $K[q]^m=K^{m+q}$ with differential $(-1)^q d_K$. For coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ placed in degree zero, define the global derived morphism groups

$$\operatorname{Ext}^q_Y(\mathcal F,\mathcal G):=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y))}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G[q]),\qquad q\ge0.$$

On $X$, these groups can be computed from a bounded cochain complex $P^\bullet$ of finite-rank locally free sheaves together with a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to\mathcal F$, by $H^q(R\Gamma(X,\mathcal H om^\bullet(P^\bullet,\mathcal G)))$; the analogous computation applies to the analytified resolution on $X^{an}$.

Define analytification by $\operatorname{An}_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F^{an}:=\eta^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{\eta^{-1}\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_{X^{an}}$. It is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence from coherent algebraic $\mathcal O_X$-modules (locally finitely presented modules) to coherent analytic $\mathcal O_{X^{an}}$-modules (locally finitely presented modules). For every coherent $\mathcal F$, the canonical cohomology comparison

$$\gamma^q_{\mathcal F}:H^q(X,\mathcal F)=R^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q(X^{an},\mathcal F^{an})=R^q\Gamma(X^{an},\mathcal F^{an})$$

is an isomorphism for all $q\ge0$. For coherent $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$, the map

$$\epsilon^q_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}:\operatorname{Ext}^q_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}^q_{X^{an}}(\mathcal F^{an},\mathcal G^{an})$$

is the map obtained by analytifying a finite locally free resolution of $\mathcal F$ and applying the cohomology comparisons term by term; independence of the chosen resolution makes it canonical. It is an isomorphism for all $q\ge0$, and for $q=0$ it is the usual comparison of algebraic and holomorphic morphisms. Here $H^q$ is sheaf cohomology computed by right-derived global sections using a supplied functorial injective-resolution datum.

Let $i:L_\infty\hookrightarrow X$ be the fixed hyperplane inclusion, where $L_\infty=\{z_0=0\}$, and let $i^{an}:L_\infty^{an}\hookrightarrow X^{an}$ be its analytification. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module, $i^*\mathcal F:=\mathcal O_{L_\infty}\otimes_{i^{-1}\mathcal O_X}i^{-1}\mathcal F$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $(i^*\mathcal F)^{an}\cong(i^{an})^*(\mathcal F^{an})$, so restriction to the fixed hyperplane commutes with analytification.

For the family clause, let $S$ be a finite-type complex scheme, put $Y=X\times S$, and let $p:Y\to S$ be projection. Write $\eta_S:S^{an}\to S$ and $\eta_Y:Y^{an}\to Y$ for analytification; then $Y^{an}\cong X^{an}\times S^{an}$, with analytic projection $p^{an}:Y^{an}\to S^{an}$. Let $\mathcal E$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module flat over $S$, meaning that for every $y\in Y$ the stalk $\mathcal E_y$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,p(y)}$. For each closed point $s\in S$ with residue field $\kappa(s)=\mathbb C$, let $j_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ be its inclusion, $X_s:=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, $i_s:X_s\hookrightarrow Y$, $p_s:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ the projection, and $\mathcal E_s:=i_s^*\mathcal E$. Let $t\in S^{an}$ be the corresponding analytic point, with inclusion $j_t:\{t\}\to S^{an}$, fiber $X_t^{an}:=Y^{an}\times_{S^{an}}\{t\}$, inclusion $i_t^{an}:X_t^{an}\hookrightarrow Y^{an}$, projection $p_t^{an}:X_t^{an}\to\{t\}$, and $\mathcal E_t^{an}:=(i_t^{an})^*\mathcal E^{an}$. For a morphism $f$ of ringed spaces, write $R^qf_*$ for the $q$th cohomology sheaf of the derived direct image computed from a supplied functorial injective resolution; on an open $V$ of the target, $(f_*I)(V)=I(f^{-1}V)$. The canonical algebraic base-change map

$$\beta^{alg}_{q,s}:(R^qp_*\mathcal E)\otimes_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s)\longrightarrow H^q(X_s,\mathcal E_s)$$

is the cohomology-and-base-change map induced by the derived base-change morphism $Lj_s^*Rp_*\mathcal E\to R(p_s)_*Li_s^*\mathcal E$, where $L(-)^*$ is the left-derived pullback functor, after the canonical edge identification $(R^qp_*\mathcal E)\otimes\kappa(s)\cong H^q(Lj_s^*Rp_*\mathcal E)$ when the direct-image cohomology sheaves in the relevant degrees are locally free. Define $\beta^{an}_{q,t}:(R^qp^{an}_*\mathcal E^{an})\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S^{an}}}\kappa(t)\to H^q(X_t^{an},\mathcal E_t^{an})$ by the analogous analytic derived base-change morphism and edge identification. Define the canonical comparison

$$c_q:(R^qp_*\mathcal E)^{an}\longrightarrow R^qp^{an}_*\mathcal E^{an}$$

by the following construction. For every algebraic open $V\subseteq S$, the morphism $\eta_Y^{-1}\mathcal E\to\mathcal E^{an}$ and the natural pullback map on sheaf cohomology give a map $H^q(p^{-1}V,\mathcal E)\to H^q((p^{an})^{-1}(\eta_S^{-1}V),\mathcal E^{an})$. These maps are compatible with restriction, so they induce a morphism from the sheafification of the first cohomology presheaf, identified with $R^qp_*\mathcal E$, to $\eta_{S*}R^qp^{an}_*\mathcal E^{an}$. The adjoint of this morphism under $\eta_S^{-1}(-)\otimes_{\eta_S^{-1}\mathcal O_S}\mathcal O_{S^{an}}\dashv\eta_{S*}$ is $c_q$. Whenever the direct-image cohomology sheaves are locally free of finite rank and both base-change maps $\beta^{alg}_{q,s}$ and $\beta^{an}_{q,t}$ are isomorphisms for every such $s$ and its corresponding $t$, $c_q$ is an isomorphism; on each fiber its induced map commutes with the two base-change maps and the absolute cohomology comparison $\gamma^q_{\mathcal E_s}$. No assertion is made that an arbitrary holomorphic family over a nonproper algebraic base algebraizes.

Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

Assume AC. Let $E$ be a smooth finite-rank complex vector bundle on a finite-dimensional complex manifold, and let $D''$ be a smooth complex-linear operator from its smooth sections to smooth $E$-valued $(0,1)$-forms satisfying $D''(fs)=\bar\partial f\otimes s+fD''s$. Extend it to bundle-valued forms by the graded Leibniz rule and suppose $(D'')^2=0$. Near every point there is a smooth invertible frame matrix $G$ with $D''G=0$. The changes between these frames are holomorphic, defining a unique holomorphic vector-bundle structure with Dolbeault operator $D''$. A smooth bundle map intertwines two such operators exactly when it is holomorphic for these structures. The construction is local and requires no projective GAGA, coherence or global vanishing theorem.

Assume full AC and DC. Let $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$, let $G=\operatorname{Gr}(2,4)$ be the complex Grassmannian of projective lines in $Z$, and let
$$\mathscr L=\{(g,z)\in G\times Z:z\in g\},\qquad p(g,z)=g,\qquad e(g,z)=z$$
be the universal line family and its projections. Let $\mathcal E\to Z$ be a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle, $N\geq2$, with the positive Ward reality datum from the preceding “Zero-FI regular ADHM and framed twistor data” definition: a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$, linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second, satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $\sigma$ is the fixed antiholomorphic involution on $Z$. For each real line $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$, where $\pi:Z\to S^4$ is the twistor projection fixed in that definition, the pairing defines $h_x(s,t)=b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ on $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$, independent of $z\in L_x$; assume $h_x$ is positive definite and $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is holomorphically trivial. Equip its fibers with the metric transported from $h_x$ by evaluation, as in that definition. Let $L_\infty=\pi^{-1}(\infty)$ and fix a unitary trivialization $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong\mathcal O_{L_\infty}^{\oplus N}$ for this metric. Write $p^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $e^{\mathrm{an}}$ for the induced analytic maps. Identify $S^4$ with its real-line locus in $G$, write $g_x\in G$ for the line parameter corresponding to $x\in S^4$, and put $\mathcal H=(p^{\mathrm{an}})_*(e^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal E$.

Let $\operatorname{ev}:(p^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal H\to(e^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal E$ be the canonical evaluation morphism, which evaluates a family of holomorphic sections at the point of its line.

Then, for every real line $L_x$, the canonical degree-zero analytic base-change map
$$\beta^0_{g_x}:\mathcal H_{g_x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{G^{\mathrm{an}},g_x}}\mathbb C(g_x)\longrightarrow H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$$
is an isomorphism, where $\mathbb C(g_x)=\mathcal O_{G^{\mathrm{an}},g_x}/\mathfrak m_{g_x}\cong\mathbb C$ is the residue field. The restriction $\mathcal H|_{S^4}$ is a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with fibre $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ at $x$, and evaluation identifies its pullback to the real incidence family with $(e^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal E$. More precisely, for every real line there is a complex-open neighbourhood in $G$ on whose entire universal-line family the evaluation morphism is an isomorphism. The framing on $L_\infty$ induces a unitary framing of this bundle at $\infty$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ bundle, $N\ge2$, with a smooth unitary connection $A$ and a unitary framing $\Phi:E_\infty\to\mathbb C^N$. Its curvature $F_A$ is an anti-Hermitian endomorphism-valued two-form; set $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$, where $*_g$ is the Hodge star for the stated metric and orientation, and assume $F_A^+=0$. The determinant-line connection is the connection induced by $A$ on $\det E=\Lambda^N E$. Its framing at $\infty$ determines a unit vector in $(\det E)_\infty$. With

$$q_N(E,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$$

and determinant Chern-form convention $c(A)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$, one has

$$q_N(E,A)=-\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle\in-\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.$$

Thus $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$ is a nonnegative integer, with the sign corresponding to the anti-self-dual equation $F_A^+=0$.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be a closed $R$-oriented smooth $n$-manifold, where $R=\mathbb Z$ or $\mathbb F_2$, and let $Z\subseteq M$ be a closed $R$-oriented embedded $z$-submanifold. Put $r=n-z$ and orient $
u_Z=TM|_Z/TZ$ in tangent-first order: $\det TM|_Z=\det TZ\otimes\det
u_Z$. Choose a smooth metric and a tubular chart whose differential induces the identity on this normal quotient; restrict to a sufficiently small closed disk bundle. Such normalized charts exist by the construction in [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]].

The normalized Thom class $u_
u\in H^r(D(
u),S(
u);R)$ corresponds to a class $\alpha\in H^r(M,M\setminus Z;R)$ by the punctured-fibre comparison and tubular excision. Write $ ar\alpha\in H^r(M;R)$ for its relative-to-absolute image. Then
$$ ar\alpha\cap[M]=(-1)^{rz}(i_Z)_*[Z]\in H_z(M;R).$$
Equivalently, $ ar\alpha=(-1)^{rz}D_M^{-1}((i_Z)_*[Z])$. The sign is the shuffle from tangent-first coordinates to normal-first cap evaluation. Over $\mathbb F_2$ all orientations are canonical and the sign disappears. A relative class capped directly with the absolute $[M]$ instead has relative homology as target; the displayed formula uses $ ar\alpha$.

Assume AC. For every $N\geq0$ identify
$\mathbb{CP}^N=\operatorname{Gr}_1(\mathbb C^{N+1})$, the space of complex
lines in $\mathbb C^{N+1}$, and let $\gamma$ be the tautological complex line
with $x=e(\gamma_{\mathbb R})\in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^N;\mathbb Z)$ its Euler class
in the complex orientation. Then, as a graded ring,
$$H^*(\mathbb{CP}^N;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[x]/(x^{N+1}),$$
the class $x$ generating each even degree and the odd groups vanishing; for
$0\leq m\leq N$ the standard inclusion
$\mathbb{CP}^m\hookrightarrow\mathbb{CP}^N$, induced by
$\mathbb C^{m+1}\subseteq\mathbb C^{N+1}$, pulls $x$ back to $x$.

derivations.claim: In the chart w=λ₂/λ₁ on a real incidence fiber, the projected horizontal (0,1) directions are H₁=∂bar_z₁−w∂z₂ and H₂=∂bar_z₂+w∂z₁. Indeed these and the vertical ∂bar_w annihilate the holomorphic coordinates w, μ₁=z₁−bar_z₂w, μ₂=z₂+bar_z₁w. They are independent and commute; their coefficients are holomorphic in w. For a unitary connection A define the pulled-back (0,1) operator by the vertical ordinary derivative and ∇_A along H₁,H₂. Its mixed squares vanish by the displayed commuting generators and holomorphic w coefficients. Its horizontal square is F_A(H₁,H₂)=F_bar1bar2−w(F_1bar1+F_2bar2)+w²F_12, which vanishes for an ASD two-form in the positive orientation: the three coefficients are precisely its self-dual component. Thus the operator squares to zero on this chart, and on the other projective chart by the same tensorial calculation. Apply [F2] to obtain a genuine holomorphic bundle. Its restriction to every real line is the constant bundle E_x, with positive reality pairing induced by the unitary metric and framing at infinity. This pairing is holomorphic: its vertical derivative vanishes on the constant fibres, and differentiating horizontally gives zero by the original identity ∇_A h=0, with the conjugate pullback at σ interchanging the conjugate horizontal directions.

For any Ward bundle use [F3] to form the analytic vector bundle H over a complex-open neighborhood U of every real line in G=Gr(2,4), with holomorphic evaluation p*H≅e*E on the universal family. On a graph chart X:A→B, incidence is (X,[λ])↦[λ,Xλ]. The distribution D=ker(de) consists of matrix variations v with vλ=0 and no λ variation. It is a holomorphic involutive rank-two subbundle, since it is tangent to the fibers of the submersion e. The restriction of p*Ω¹_U to D has kernel B*⊗O(-1) on each projective-line fiber and target D*≅O(1)². The O(-1) vanishings in [F3] give Ω¹_U≅p_*D*. Equivalently, on the graph chart a linear covector on Hom(A,B) restricts to a section on all kernels vλ=0; the map is injective because those kernels span Hom(A,B), and both coefficient spaces have dimension four. This gives the holomorphic sheaf isomorphism without any extra analytic base-change assumption.

The bundle e*E has a canonical flat partial connection δ along D: in a holomorphic frame pulled back from E, differentiate coefficient functions along the fibers of e. Changes of that frame have zero D derivative, so δ is well-defined and flat. Transfer δ to p*H by evaluation. For a local holomorphic section s of H, δ(p*s) is a section of D*⊗p*H. Push down using Ω¹_U≅p_*D* from step 2.1 to define ∇s. The partial Leibniz rule becomes ∇(fs)=df⊗s+f∇s, so ∇ is a holomorphic full connection. Its pullback restriction to D is δ, first on pulled-back sections and then on all sections by Leibniz. It is unique: the difference of two such connections is an End(H)-valued one-form restricting to zero on D at every λ, hence zero by the same cotangent isomorphism. The curvature restricts on D to δ²=0. Connections on overlapping graph charts agree by uniqueness.

Restrict H and ∇ to the totally real graph locus M=HP¹. Its smooth real incidence is diffeomorphic to Z by (P,[v])↦[v], with inverse [v]↦(span(v,jv),[v]); the explicit charts in [F3] verify smoothness. Under this identification dp(D) is exactly the span of H₁,H₂ in step 1.1: write X_z=((z₁,-bar_z₂),(z₂,bar_z₁)) and solve v(1,w)^T=0. Therefore the restricted smooth connection has F(H₁,H₂)=0 for every w, so all three self-dual coefficients in step 1.1 vanish. Hence it is ASD. Evaluation intertwines the original holomorphic operator on E with the reconstructed vertical/horizontal Dolbeault operator: it is holomorphic vertically, and on D its derivative is exactly the canonical relative derivative δ by step 3.1. These directions generate the (0,1) tangent in step 1.1, proving equality of the full operators, not just of underlying bundles.

To identify the connection with the first-neighborhood prescription, the line's conormal bundle is O(-1)², by its two independent linear defining equations. The sequence 0→E|L⊗(I/I²)→E|L^(1)→E|L→0 and [F3]'s O(-1) vanishings give a unique extension of every line section to L^(1). Smooth variation is supplied by step 3.1, not merely inferred from this pointwise uniqueness. At a graph X choose a local holomorphic section s of H with specified value and ∇s(X)=0; in a local frame its affine-linear coefficient function can realize any prescribed first jet. Its evaluation derivative in parameter direction v vanishes on vλ=0 by step 3.1, so factors through the normal displacement vλ. These factorizations glue on the two λ charts and give precisely a first-neighborhood extension. Uniqueness identifies it with the preceding extension. Subtracting such a horizontal first jet from an arbitrary section shows that differentiation relative to this extension is exactly ∇. This proves the prescription, its Leibniz rule, chart independence and smooth dependence.

The section metric is the form induced by b_z(s(z),t(σz)) in [F1]. It is independent of z on each line because that scalar is holomorphic on P¹, and is smooth by the evaluation frames of [F3]. The preceding construction commutes with duals, conjugate pullback and bundle morphisms: each commutes with the canonical relative e-connection and the cotangent isomorphism, and uniqueness in step 3.1 then forces the full connections to commute. Apply this to the holomorphic reality isomorphism E→σ*bar_E*. On the real line locus, the induced conjugate involution fixes the parameter and its real tangent vectors. Thus the induced map H→bar_H* intertwines ∇ with the conjugate dual connection, which is precisely X h(s,t)=h(∇_X s,t)+h(s,∇_X t) for real X. Positivity from [F1] makes ∇ unitary. Arbitrary independent positive forms would not satisfy this identity and are not used.

Starting from A in step 1.1, its constant real-line sections identify the reconstructed smooth H with E. Along every alpha-plane the recovered connection has the same derivative as A; the cotangent uniqueness in step 3.1 makes the full connections equal. The unitary reality pairing and framing also agree. Starting from a Ward bundle, step 4.1 proves evaluation is a holomorphic isomorphism from the reconstructed pullback to the original bundle, and step 5.2 preserves its reality pairing and metric. These constructions and identities apply to morphisms as well, so descend to inverse maps on based unitary gauge and framed holomorphic isomorphism classes. No irreducibility or absence of parallel sections was used.

The explicit incidence chart fixes vertical complex orientation followed by the positive base orientation to be the complex orientation of Z. The pullback of the positive point Thom class on S⁴ is the positive normal Thom class of its fiber CP¹; [F5] identifies its absolute class as the Poincaré dual of that fiber. Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and let $X$
be a smooth equidimensional $k$-scheme of finite type
([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]), with Chow ring $A^*(X)$
([[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]) and
vector-bundle group $K^0(X)$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]).
When $X$ is additionally quasi-projective,
[[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]] identifies this group with
coherent $K_0(X)$; that extra hypothesis is required for the coherent-group
extension. Write $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}:=A^*(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$. If $n=\dim X$,
$A^i(X)=A_{n-i}(X)=0$ for $i>n$, since there are no negative-dimensional
integral cycles. Every series below is evaluated only through degree $n$;
in particular positive-codimension elements are nilpotent. For the rank-zero
bundle the empty root list gives $\operatorname{ch}(0)=0$ and
$\operatorname{td}(0)=1$.

**Chern roots.** The **Chern roots** of a finite locally free
$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ are formal symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_r$ with the property that the elementary symmetric functions in the
$x_i$ are the Chern classes: $e_i(x_1,\dots,x_r)=c_i(\mathcal E)$
([[def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle]]); by the splitting principle every
symmetric polynomial expression in the $x_i$ with rational coefficients defines
a well-defined element of $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$
([[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]]).

**Chern character.** Define
$$\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E):=\sum_{j=1}^{r}e^{x_j}=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac{1}{m!}\,p_m(c_1,\dots,c_m)\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q},$$
where $p_0:=r=\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E$, while for $m\ge1$ the
power sum $p_m(c_1,\dots,c_m)=\sum_jx_j^m$ is a universal polynomial in
the Chern classes. Thus $\operatorname{ch}_0(\mathcal E)=r$; explicitly
$\operatorname{ch}=r+c_1+\tfrac12(c_1^2-2c_2)+\tfrac16(c_1^3-3c_1c_2+3c_3)+\cdots$
(the denominators are why we tensor with $\mathbb Q$).

**Todd class.** Define
$$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E):=\prod_{j=1}^{r}\frac{x_j}{1-e^{-x_j}}\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q};$$
explicitly
$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E)=1+\tfrac12c_1+\tfrac1{12}(c_1^2+c_2)+\tfrac1{24}c_1c_2+\cdots$.
For a smooth $X$ the **Todd class of $X$** is $\operatorname{td}(T_X)$ for the
tangent bundle $T_X=\operatorname{Hom}(\Omega^1_{X/k},\mathcal O_X)$
([[def-sheaf-relative-differentials]],
[[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]]).

**Line bundles.** For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ with
$x=c_1(\mathcal L)$: $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal L)=e^{x}$ and
$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal L)=x/(1-e^{-x})=1+\tfrac12x+\tfrac1{12}x^2-\cdots$.

**Well-definedness.** After truncation at degree $n$, the positive-degree
components of the Chern character and all components of the Todd class are
symmetric polynomials with rational coefficients in the Chern roots, hence
universal polynomial expressions in their elementary symmetric functions,
the Chern classes of [[def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle]]. The degree-zero
component of the Chern character is the rank $r$. Thus the Chern character
depends only on the rank and Chern classes of $\mathcal E$, whereas the Todd
class depends only on its Chern classes. For locally constant ranks these
formulas are interpreted componentwise on the finite open-and-closed rank
loci. By the splitting principle of
[[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]], these values are
independent of the choice of flag bundle or filtration: any two filtrations
have the same rank and elementary symmetric functions, and hence give the
same polynomial values. Rational coefficients are needed for
the exponential and geometric expansions, which is why the target is
$A^*(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$. The tangent bundle is finite locally free
of rank $\dim X$ by [[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]], so its Chern
roots and Todd class are defined; the Todd class is multiplicative in exact sequences, whereas the Chern
character is additive, and the
identification of $K^0(X)$ with $K_0(X)$ on a quasi-projective $X$ lets the
character be evaluated on coherent classes through the finite locally free
resolutions of [[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]].

Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

u_Z=TM|_Z/TZ$ in tangent-first order: $\det TM|_Z=\det TZ\otimes\det
u_Z$. Choose a smooth metric and a tubular chart whose differential induces the identity on this normal quotient; restrict to a sufficiently small closed disk bundle. Such normalized charts exist by the construction in [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]].

The normalized Thom class $u_
u\in H^r(D(
u),S(
u);R)$ corresponds to a class $\alpha\in H^r(M,M\setminus Z;R)$ by the punctured-fibre comparison and tubular excision. Write $ ar\alpha\in H^r(M;R)$ for its relative-to-absolute image. Then

$$H^*(\mathbb{CP}^N;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[x]/(x^{N+1}),$$

second-countable smooth manifold, possibly with boundary or empty, and let
$\rho_M:H^*(M;\mathbb Z)\to H^*(M;\mathbb R)$ be induced by
$\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$. Write $J_M$ for the natural de Rham
isomorphism from real de Rham cohomology to singular cohomology with real

For every finite-rank smooth real bundle $V\to M$ with any real connection

$$J_M([p_j(D)])=\rho_M(p_j(V)).$$

$$J_M([e(\nabla)])=\rho_M(e(W)).$$

derivations.claim: In the Grothendieck group, exactness of the monad gives $[\mathcal E]=(2k+N)[\mathcal O]-k[\mathcal O(-1)]-k[\mathcal O(1)]$. By [F1], its Chern character is $(2k+N)-ke^{-H}-ke^H=N-kH^2$, because the constant terms cancel to $N$, the linear terms cancel, the quadratic contribution is $-kH^2$, and terms of degree at least four vanish on $Z$. Therefore $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$ and $c_2(\mathcal E)=-\operatorname{ch}_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$.

Let $x\in S^4$. In the explicit incidence chart of the Definition, $\mu_1=z_1$, $\mu_2=z_2$ at $\lambda_2=0$, so the vertical complex orientation followed by the positive stereographic orientation is the complex orientation on $Z$. The submersion pulls the oriented normal disk at $x$ back to the normal disk of its fibre; fibrewise normalization and uniqueness of the Thom class, followed by its relative-to-absolute map, therefore pull the positive point dual to the positive fibre dual. The class $u$ is Poincaré dual to the positively oriented point $x$, so $\pi^*u$ is Poincaré dual to the fibre $L_x$. By [F2] that fibre has its complex line orientation; as a linear $\mathbb CP^1\subset\mathbb CP^3$ its Poincaré dual is $H^2$, since $\int_{L_x}H=1$ and $H^2$ generates degree-four cohomology. The twistor orientation clause in the Definition makes this the positive pullback class, hence $\pi^*u=H^2$.

Write $c_2(E)=m u$ for the integer $m=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$. Naturality and the Ward pullback in the Statement give $mH^2=\pi^*c_2(E)=c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$ by step 1.1 and step 1.2. Since $H^2$ is nonzero, $m=k$. Finally [F3] gives $-q_N=m=k$, with the nonnegative sign fixed by the ASD equation.

boundaries.evidence: At k=0 both outer monad terms O(-1)^0 and O(1)^0 are zero bundles. The middle term is O^N and its cohomology remains O^N; Proof 1.1 reduces the K-class formula to ch=N, c_2=0.
Proof 1.1 has ch=N-kH^2 and Proof 2.1 has -q_N=k. Setting k=0 gives zero c_2 and zero framed charge; the vanishing outer terms leave the rank-N trivial middle cohomology, not an empty bundle.

At k=1 the monad has outer line bundles O(-1), O(1) and middle rank N+2. Proof 1.1 gives c_2=H^2, and the positive pullback calculation in Proof 1.2–2.1 gives q_N=-1, conditional on the stated monad and ASD input.

Zero multiplicity k=0 is compatible with a monad because the zero outer maps satisfy its end exactness conditions; for k>0 the Statement still requires a genuine monad and Ward ASD identification. Arbitrary rank-defective complexes are not substituted for those hypotheses.

boundaries.reason: The fixed oriented fibration CP3 -> S4 has no FI or scale-chamber parameter. Proof 1.2 fixes the positive sign of pi*u=H^2 using orientation rather than taking a parameter endpoint.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

$$\beta^0_{g_x}:\mathcal H_{g_x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{G^{\mathrm{an}},g_x}}\mathbb C(g_x)\longrightarrow H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$$
is an isomorphism, where $\mathbb C(g_x)=\mathcal O_{G^{\mathrm{an}},g_x}/\mathfrak m_{g_x}\cong\mathbb C$ is the residue field. The restriction $\mathcal H|_{S^4}$ is a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with fibre $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ at $x$, and evaluation identifies its pullback to the real incidence family with $(e^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal E$. More precisely, for every real line there is a complex-open neighbourhood in $G$ on whose entire universal-line family the evaluation morphism is an isomorphism. The framing on $L_\infty$ induces a unitary framing of this bundle at $\infty$.

Assume full AC and the following exact projective GAGA comparison: analytification on $\mathbb P^3_{\mathbb C}$ is an exact tensor equivalence on coherent sheaves and induces cohomology isomorphisms. The local smooth integrable-Dolbeault frame theorem is supplied by the explicit local proof below, rather than assumed as a new analytic input.

For integers $k\ge0$, $N\ge2$, let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$. A framed ASD object is a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ bundle $E\to S^4$, a smooth unitary connection $A$, a unitary framing at infinity, $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$, and $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)=-k$, modulo unitary bundle isomorphisms preserving the connection and framing; write $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ for this set.

Set $Z=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$, let $j$ be the fixed right quaternionic structure with $j^2=-1$, and define $\sigma([v])=[jv]$ and $\pi([v])=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}(v,jv)\in\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$. For $x\in S^4$, the real twistor line is $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $L_\infty$ is the fiber over infinity. A positive Hermitian Ward reality datum on a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle $\mathcal E\to Z$ is a nondegenerate holomorphic pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$ and such that

$$h_x(s,t)=b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$$

is independent of $z\in L_x$ and positive definite on $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$. A unitary framing on $L_\infty$ is an isomorphism $\Phi:\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{L_\infty}^{\oplus N}$ that is unitary for the form induced by $b$. Let $\mathcal O_Z(1)$ be the dual tautological line bundle, put $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$, and require $\mathcal E|_{L_x}\cong\mathcal O_{L_x}^{\oplus N}$ for every real twistor line and $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$.

Then $\widehat E_x=H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ forms a smooth rank-$N$ Hermitian bundle on $S^4$. For the ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_{L_x}$ of $L_x$, its first infinitesimal neighbourhood is the closed subscheme with structure sheaf $\mathcal O_Z/\mathcal I_{L_x}^2$. Extend each section of $\widehat E_x$ holomorphically and uniquely to that neighbourhood and differentiate the extension in the family of lines; this defines the Ward connection $\widehat\nabla$. The form induced by $b$ is smooth and is preserved by $\widehat\nabla$; this is a conclusion, not an independent metric-compatibility assumption.

Use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ with rank-two complex spinor bundles $S^+$ and $S^-$, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. A point of $L_x=\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is a complex line $\ell\subset S_x^+$, and $\ell\otimes S_x^-$ is the corresponding complex alpha-plane. Under these hypotheses, the Ward construction gives a bijection between the framed ASD classes in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ and isomorphism classes of the specified framed Ward data, where Ward isomorphisms preserve the holomorphic bundle, pairing $b$, and framing $\Phi$. The reconstructed Ward connection satisfies $F^+=0$ and $q_N=-k$. The inverse sends a framed ASD connection to the holomorphic structure on $\pi^*E$ whose vertical part is the standard Dolbeault operator and whose horizontal $(0,1)$ part is induced by $A$ along the horizontal lifts of vectors in these alpha-planes, using the Levi-Civita horizontal distribution of $\pi$. Define $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$, with $S^1=\{u\in\mathbb C:|u|=1\}$, $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N\in S^1$, and $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. It acts on $S^4$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$, on framed ASD classes by inverse pullback and postcomposition of the framing by $h$, and on $Z$ by $g([\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2])=[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$; the induced action on framed Ward data is inverse pullback by $g$ together with postcomposition of $\Phi$ by $h$. Both maps preserve the framing, Hermitian form, charge, and these torus actions. Reducible bundles and flat summands are included; no irreducibility assumption is imposed.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ bundle, $N\ge2$, with a smooth unitary connection $A$ and a unitary framing $\Phi:E_\infty\to\mathbb C^N$. Its curvature $F_A$ is an anti-Hermitian endomorphism-valued two-form; set $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$, where $*_g$ is the Hodge star for the stated metric and orientation, and assume $F_A^+=0$. The determinant-line connection is the connection induced by $A$ on $\det E=\Lambda^N E$. Its framing at $\infty$ determines a unit vector in $(\det E)_\infty$. With

$$q_N(E,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$$

and determinant Chern-form convention $c(A)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$, one has

$$q_N(E,A)=-\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle\in-\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.$$

Thus $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$ is a nonnegative integer, with the sign corresponding to the anti-self-dual equation $F_A^+=0$.

Assume full AC. Let $S^4$ have the unit round metric and the positive stereographic orientation for $z_1=x_0+ix_1$, $z_2=x_2+ix_3$. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth finite-rank complex vector bundle with a positive Hermitian metric $h$ and a smooth connection $\nabla_A$ preserving $h$. Its curvature is $F_A=\nabla_A^2\in\Omega^2(S^4,\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}E)$. For real two-forms $\eta,\zeta$, let $*_g$ be characterized by $\eta\wedge *_g\zeta=\langle\eta,\zeta\rangle_g\,d\mathrm{vol}_g$, and extend it complex-linearly on the form factor of $F_A$. Set $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$ and assume $F_A^+=0$, the anti-self-duality condition in this orientation. On $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ use homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ and the incidence equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$, with infinity fibre $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$; these fibres define the incidence projection $\pi:Z\to S^4$. On $\lambda_1\ne0$, put $t=\lambda_2/\lambda_1$, $H_1=\partial_{\bar z_1}-t\partial_{z_2}$, and $H_2=\partial_{\bar z_2}+t\partial_{z_1}$. The projected complex alpha-plane at $[\lambda]\in\pi^{-1}(x)$ is $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{d\pi(H_1),d\pi(H_2)\}$; the second projective chart covers $t=\infty$. Let $\mathcal O_Z(-1)$ be the tautological holomorphic line bundle and $\mathcal O_Z(-2)=\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\otimes2}$. Suppose $F$ is a finite-rank holomorphic bundle (locally trivial with holomorphic transition maps), smoothly identified with $\pi^*E$, and its Dolbeault operator is the coefficientwise ordinary vertical operator and the connection $\nabla_A$ on the projected complex alpha-planes. For a finite-rank holomorphic bundle $G\to Z$, write $H^1(Z,G)$ for analytic sheaf cohomology of its holomorphic-section sheaf; under the analytic Dolbeault comparison it is canonically $\ker(\bar\partial_G:\Omega^{0,1}(Z,G)\to\Omega^{0,2}(Z,G))/\operatorname{im}(\bar\partial_G:\Omega^{0,0}(Z,G)\to\Omega^{0,1}(Z,G))$, where $\Omega^{0,q}(Z,G)$ denotes the global smooth $G$-valued $(0,q)$-forms. Write $F^\vee$ for the fibrewise complex dual. Then

$$H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))=H^1(Z,F^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))=0.$$

This applies to arbitrary reducible and flat summands. It assumes no algebraic-to-analytic GAGA, monad, or inverse ADHM normal form as an independent premise.
For every natural number $n\ge2$, the unit sphere $S^n\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ is simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]).

A connection on a finite-rank smooth vector bundle $E\to M$ is flat if and
only if every point of $M$ has a neighborhood carrying a local frame
$(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ of parallel sections, meaning $\nabla_Xe_a=0$ for every
local vector field $X$ and every $a$.

Let $E\to M$ carry a flat connection, meaning $R^\nabla=0$. For every
$p\in M$ there is a coordinate ball $U$ about $p$ such that, whenever two
piecewise smooth paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to U$ have the same initial
and terminal points,

$$P_{\gamma_0}=P_{\gamma_1}.$$

This is a local assertion; it makes no claim about transport around loops in a
non-simply-connected larger domain.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. A section $s$ of a rank-$d$
bundle $Q$ is a **regular section** here if, at each point of its zero scheme
$Z(s)$, some local frame expresses $s$ by $d$ components forming a regular
sequence of length $d$ in the local ring. Under this hypothesis it has exact
Koszul resolution
$\bigwedge^dQ^\vee\to\cdots\to Q^\vee\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_{Z(s)}\to0$.
Tensoring with a vector bundle preserves it. If a coherent sheaf $H$ has a
finite locally free resolution on a scheme and $t$ is a Cartier equation acting
injectively on $H$, restricting the resolution to $t=0$ remains exact and
resolves $H/tH$. In the deformation blowup for a closed embedding of smooth
quasi-projective varieties $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$, let $E$ be a finite
locally free sheaf on $X$. The strict transform
$F:X\times\mathbb P^1\hookrightarrow M$ is disjoint from
$B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, and a resolution of $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$
restricts exactly to the ordinary $Y$ fibre and to
$P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(N\oplus1)$; on $B$ it is an exact complex.

For an additive left-exact functor $F$ and a bounded-below complex $K$ with supplied Cartan–Eilenberg resolution $I$, there is a spectral sequence
$$E_1^{p,q}=R^qF(K^p)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathbb R_I^{p+q}F(K),\qquad d_r:(p,q)\mapsto(p+r,q-r+1).$$
Here $q\ge0$ and $p\ge b$ if $K^p=0$ for $p<b$. It is first quadrant after translating $p$ by $b$ and converges strongly with a finite filtration on every target degree. Derived objects use the supplied columns; under DC, or supplied Cartan–Eilenberg comparison and homotopy data, it is natural in $K$ and independent of the resolution from $E_1$ onward.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge0$, let
$X=\mathbb P^n_k$ with dualizing line bundle $\omega_X=\mathcal O(-n-1)$ and
residue trace $t_X:H^n(X,\omega_X)\to k$
([[def-smooth-projective-dualizing-line-bundle-and-trace]]), and let
$\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}$ be the global sheaf Ext of
[[def-sheaf-ext-for-coherent-modules]].

1. **(The pairing.)** For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, every
   $q\in\{0,\dots,n\}$, $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)$
   and $\eta\in H^q(X,F)$ set
   $$\langle\alpha,\eta\rangle_F\;:=\;t_X\Bigl(\chi^n_{\omega_X}\bigl(\alpha\cdot\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)\bigr)\Bigr),$$
   where $\chi^q_F:\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q(X,F)$
   is the canonical isomorphism of
   [[lem-injective-modules-flasque-and-ext-of-structure-sheaf]],
   $\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)$ is the corresponding class in
   $\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,F)$, and
   $\alpha\cdot\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^n_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,\omega_X)$
   is the Yoneda product of
   $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)$ with
   $\beta=\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)$, i.e. composition
   $\alpha\circ\beta$ of derived morphisms under
   $\operatorname{Ext}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal O_X}(-,-)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X))}(-,-[\bullet])$
   ([[thm-ext-is-hom-in-the-derived-category]],
   [[prop-yoneda-product-is-composition-in-the-derived-category]]). This
   **Serre duality pairing** is $k$-bilinear and natural in $F$.

2. **(Perfectness.)** For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ and every
   $q\in\{0,\dots,n\}$ the pairing
   $$\langle-,-\rangle_F:\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\times H^q(X,F)\longrightarrow k$$
   is a perfect pairing of $k$-vector spaces, i.e. both adjoint maps
   $\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\to H^q(X,F)^\vee$ and
   $H^q(X,F)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)^\vee$ are
   isomorphisms.

The case $q=n$ of clause 2 is the classical statement that
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\to H^n(X,F)^\vee$,
$\varphi\mapsto(\eta\mapsto t_X(H^n(\varphi)(\eta)))$, is an isomorphism, and
for $F=\mathcal O_X$ clause 2 recovers $H^{n-q}(X,\omega_X)\cong H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)^\vee$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. Let $k$ be an algebraically
closed field, let $Y$ be a nonsingular equidimensional quasi-projective
$k$-scheme of finite type ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]],
[[cor-smooth-variety-classical-scheme-conventions-agree]]), let $n\ge0$ and let
$$p:\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY\longrightarrow Y$$
be the projection. For every
$\alpha\in K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]):
$$\operatorname{ch}\bigl(p_!(\alpha)\bigr)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\;=\;p_*\Bigl(\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n\times_kY})\Bigr)\qquad\text{in }A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q},$$
where $\operatorname{ch},\operatorname{td}$ are the Chern character and Todd
class of [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]], $p_!$ is the K-theory
pushforward ([[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]],
[[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]) and $p_*$ is the proper
pushforward on Chow groups
([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]). Equivalently, writing
$\tau_X(\alpha)=\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\operatorname{td}(T_X)$, the diagram
$$\begin{array}{ccc}K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY) & \xrightarrow{\ \tau\ } & A^*(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)_{\mathbb Q}\\ \downarrow p_! & & \downarrow p_*\\ K_0(Y) & \xrightarrow{\ \tau\ } & A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\end{array}$$
commutes. The case $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch for
$\mathbb P^n$, and the case of a general projective-bundle projection is obtained
by the same argument applied to the projective bundle formula.

Let $m \ge 1$, let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}^m$ be a nonempty connected open set,
and let $f : U \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic
([[def-holomorphic-function-in-several-complex-variables]]). If there is a
nonempty open set $W \subseteq U$ such that $f(z) = 0$ for every $z \in W$, then
$f \equiv 0$ on $U$.

This is the several-variable identity theorem at the strength the page supports:
the hypothesis is a nonempty **open** set of zeros. An accumulation point of the
zero set is neither assumed nor sufficient in several variables; the companion
page records that stronger one-variable statement as false here.

derivations.claim: The Ward construction gives exactly the smooth pullback bundle and vertical/horizontal Dolbeault operator required in [A1], for the same sphere and incidence in [F1]. Thus its two cohomology vanishings apply directly. The dual is again unitary and ASD, since its curvature is $-F_A^t$ and Hodge star commutes with transpose, and its holomorphic operator is the induced dual one. Hence both $H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))$ and $H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))$ vanish. This uses the supplier's exact stated conclusion, not an unexposed injective-map premise.

Let $L\cong\mathbb P^1$ be any real twistor line. Its normal bundle in $\mathbb P^3$ is $\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$, and the conormal sequence splits because its extension group is $H^1(\mathcal O(1))^{\oplus2}=0$. Hence $\Omega_Z^1|_L\cong\mathcal O(-2)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2}$ and $T_Z|_L\cong\mathcal O(2)\oplus\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$. Since $\Omega_Z^2\cong T_Z(-4)$, each of $\mathcal E(-1)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-3)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-2)|_L$, $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))|_L$, and $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)|_L$ is a sum of negative line bundles. The Serre-dual bundles restrict respectively to $\mathcal E^*(-3)$, $\mathcal E^*(-1)$, $\mathcal E^*(-2)$, $\mathcal E^*\otimes T_Z(-3)$, and $\mathcal E^*\otimes\Omega_Z^1$, also sums of negative line bundles. Every point of $Z$ lies on a real line, so negativity on every such line makes every global section zero. Thus [F6] gives $H^0(Z,F)=0$ and [F5] gives $H^3(Z,F)=0$ for all the listed coefficient bundles $F$.

Choose a plane $P\cong\mathbb P^2$ containing a real twistor line. By [A2] and the direct-image result, an open family of lines near that line has evaluation isomorphisms and hence trivial restrictions of $\mathcal E$. Those lines form a nonempty complex-open subset of the line family of $P$. Choose affine coordinates $(x,y)$ with the original line given by $y=0$. This open family contains the projective lines $y=b$ for all sufficiently small complex $b$, so their union contains a nonempty open subset of $P$. A section of $\mathcal E(-2)|_P$ vanishes on each such line because $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus N})=0$. It therefore vanishes on that open subset. In a connected coordinate chart and holomorphic bundle frame, [F8] makes its zero-germ locus closed as well as open. The plane is connected (any two points lie on a connected projective line), so the section vanishes everywhere; no density assertion for an arbitrary complex-open line family is needed. The divisor sequence $0\to\mathcal E(-3)\to\mathcal E(-2)\to\mathcal E(-2)|_P\to0$ and step 1.1 now give $H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-3))=0$.

Tensor $0\to\Omega_Z^1(-1)\to\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus4}\to\mathcal O(-1)\to0$ by $\mathcal E$. Step 1.2 gives $H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=H^0(\mathcal E(-1))=0$, and step 1.1 gives $H^1(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. The long exact sequence yields $H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))=0$. Serre duality and step 1.1 also give $H^2(\mathcal E(-2))=0$.

Apply [F4] to the diagonal Koszul resolution [F3], tensoring the second factor by $\mathcal E(-2)$, pushing to the first factor, and twisting that output factor by $\mathcal O(2)$. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(Z,\mathcal E(-2)\otimes\Omega_Z^{-p}(-p))\otimes\mathcal O_Z(p+2)$ for $p=-3,-2,-1,0$. Steps 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 and Serre duality make every term in rows $q=0,1,3$ vanish except possibly $H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)$ at $(-2,1)$. No differential can enter this term; its only possible outgoing $d_2$ lands in $H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. It therefore survives to $E_\infty$, but the diagonal construction resolves $\mathcal E(-2)$ before the output twist and $\mathcal E$ after that twist; it is concentrated in degree zero and has no degree $-1$ hypercohomology. Since $(-2)+1=-1$, the term is zero. Thus the remaining spectral-sequence row is $q=2$.

The row $q=2$ gives the complex $H^2(\mathcal E(-3))\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)\otimes\mathcal O\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))\otimes\mathcal O(1)$. All higher differentials vanish because all other rows are zero. Its only cohomology is the degree-zero hypercohomology of the diagonal resolution, namely $\mathcal E$; the first and last terms are exact because the other total degrees vanish. The maps are linear in the homogeneous output coordinates, since each Koszul differential is contraction with the universal linear section. Thus this is the stated monad; its cohomology vector spaces are canonical, and changing bases acts by $GL(U)\times GL(K)\times GL(U')$.

From [A3], $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E(t))=Ne^{tH}-kH^2e^{tH}$ and $\operatorname{td}(T_Z)=1+2H+\tfrac{11}{6}H^2+H^3$. Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch [F7] gives $\chi(\mathcal E(t))=N\binom{t+3}{3}-k(t+2)$, with values $k,-N+2k,0,-k$ for $t=-3,-4,-2,-1$. The Euler sequences $0\to\mathcal O(-4)\to\mathcal O(-3)^{\oplus4}\to\Omega_Z^2\to0$ and $0\to\Omega_Z^1(-1)\to\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus4}\to\mathcal O(-1)\to0$ give Euler characteristics $k,2k+N,k$ for the three monad coefficient bundles. Steps 1.2, 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1 leave only $H^2$ in each, so these values are the dimensions.

The space of parallel sections of $\widehat E$ evaluates to a trivial subbundle, and its orthogonal complement is parallel because the connection is unitary. No nonzero parallel section lies in the complement. Every flat summand is trivial since $S^4$ is simply connected [F2]. The Ward transform and diagonal construction preserve direct sums. For a trivial rank-$m$ summand $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus m}$, the two Euler sequences and [F6] give coefficient groups $H^2(\mathcal O(-3))=0$, $H^2(\Omega_Z^2)^{\oplus m}\cong\mathbb C^m$, and $H^2(\Omega_Z^1(-1))=0$, so its monad is $0\to\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus m}\to0$. Flat summands are therefore included without imposing $H^0(Z,\mathcal E)=0$ or $H^0(Z,\mathcal E^\vee)=0$. No Dirac index or kernel-dimension formula is used.
