risk_review.notes: Checked all eight steps against exact conditional inputs. Coupled vanishings apply to actual Ward operator and its dual. Negative restrictions on every real line kill H0 and Serre-dual H3. A complex-open line family in a plane gives an open swept subset; identity theorem and divisor sequence kill H1(E(-3)). Euler sequences kill the other H1, H2(E(-2)). The sole possible E1(-2,1) survivor has no incoming differential and only zero outgoing target; total degree -1 forces zero. Remaining q=2 row is the monad. RR polynomial chi(E(t))=N binom(t+3,3)-k(t+2) yields k,2k+N,k. Parallel flat summands contribute only their middle rank and are not excluded; no irreducibility or H0(E)=0 premise.

citations.quote:
Assume full AC. Let $k\ge0$ and
$N\ge2$. On $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ with homogeneous coordinates
$(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$, set
$$j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2) =(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1), \qquad \sigma([z])=[jz].$$
For each $(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$, let $\ell_z$ be the real twistor line
defined by
$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,$$
and let $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Suppose
$$\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha} \mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta} \mathcal O(1)\otimes U'$$
is a complex of holomorphic vector bundles with $\beta\alpha=0$, locally split
injective and surjective end maps, and locally free middle cohomology
$F=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ of rank $N$, where
$\dim_\mathbb C U=\dim_\mathbb C U'=k$ and
$\dim_\mathbb C S=2k+N$. Suppose $F|_{\ell_z}$ is holomorphically trivial for
every $z$, and it has a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian pairing
$h_F:F\to D(F)$ fixed by the canonical double-dual identification, where
$D(F)=(\sigma^*\overline F)^\vee$. For a $\sigma$-invariant real line $\ell$
and sections $s,t\in H^0(\ell,F|_\ell)$, the induced first-slot-linear
Hermitian form is the constant value of
$x\mapsto h_{F,x}(s(x))(\overline{t(\sigma x)})$; assume it is positive
definite. This is the line-form convention of the preceding first-order
real-structure definition. At the monad level, for a homogeneous linear
matrix $P$ set $P^\#(z)=P(jz)^\dagger$; the signed dual monad has
differentials $-\beta^\#$ and $\alpha^\#$, so its cohomology is $D(F)$ and
its double dual is the original monad under the induced identifications.
Suppose also that a
unitary framing identifies $F|_{\ell_\infty}$ isometrically with
$W\otimes\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$ for a fixed Hermitian space $W$ of dimension
$N$.

Then there are Hermitian
spaces $V$ and $W$ of dimensions $k$ and $N$, with $W$ carrying the prescribed
framing, and maps
$$B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V),\qquad I:W\to V,\qquad J:V\to W$$
such that, after a pairing-preserving framed chain identification, the monad
maps are
$$\alpha= \begin{pmatrix} A\\ C\\ J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \beta=(-C,\ A,\ I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2),$$
where
$$A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1,\qquad C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2.$$
The extracted maps satisfy both zero-moment equations
$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0.$$
They are stable, meaning the vectors
$B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$, and costable, meaning no nonzero
subspace invariant under both $B_i$ is contained in $\ker J$. Conversely,
every such regular datum with both moments zero gives a locally split monad
with the stated real-line positivity and infinity framing.
Here $\dagger$ denotes adjoint in the indicated Hermitian spaces.

In the next assertion, a normalized framed isomorphism is a chain
isomorphism preserving the lifted pairing and the specified infinity frame.
Such isomorphisms correspond exactly to the simultaneous $U(V)$ action
$$(B_1,B_2,I,J)\longmapsto (gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1}),\qquad g\in U(V).$$
Thus inverse coefficient extraction recovers precisely one $U(V)$ orbit; when
$k=0$, $U(0)$ is trivial, and every constant flat summand is retained as an
unused orthogonal subspace of $W$.

For $t_1,t_2\in U(1)$, choose an orthonormal framed basis
$w_1,\ldots,w_N$ of $W$ and phases $e_1,\ldots,e_N\in U(1)$, and let
$h(w_a)=e_a^{-1}w_a$. The coordinate action
$(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto
(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ acts on data by
$$(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto (t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ).$$
The corresponding chain factors on the source, middle and target terms are,
respectively,
$(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$, and $1$.

The same extraction and classification hold naturally for first-order
families over $A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with
$\bar\epsilon=\epsilon$ in the following exact locally-free/base-change
range: the three modules are free of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, the end maps are
locally split, the middle cohomology is locally free and commutes with
reduction, its global section module is free and commutes with reduction, the
coefficient-image submodule in the middle term is a direct summand and
commutes with reduction, and each fixed real-line restriction is trivial
with its section module commuting with reduction. The framing and pairing
are defined over $A$, while positivity is required only on the reduced
complex; adjoints on these modules use the coefficient involution and the
induced $A$-Hermitian forms. Call an $A$-valued datum regular when its
reduction is stable and costable. The extracted matrices lie over $A$ and
obey the same moment equations. Conversely, every $A$-valued regular datum
whose raw
monad satisfies these same global-section, coefficient-image and real-line
base-change conditions gives a family in this range. Pairing-preserving
framed family isomorphisms correspond exactly to
$U(k,A)=\{g:g^\dagger g=1\}$. This assertion is restricted to reduction and
the involution-preserving base maps $\epsilon\mapsto r\epsilon$ with
$r\in\mathbb R$.

For the finite algebraic monad resolution, let
$H_{\rm alg}=c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ and
$H_{\rm top}=c_1^{\rm top}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$. The hyperplane cycle
map identifies these classes in their respective theories. Then
$\operatorname{ch}(F)=N-kH_{\rm alg}^2$ and
$c_2^{\rm alg}(F)=kH_{\rm alg}^2$. Its topological line class is the same
$H_{\rm top}$ and $c_2^{\rm top}(F)=kH_{\rm top}^2$. Define
$\jmath:\mathbb C^4\to\mathbb C^4$ by
$\jmath(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$,
so $\jmath^2=-1$. Identify $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ with the set of
$\jmath$-invariant complex two-planes in $\mathbb C^4$, and define the twistor
quotient map $\pi:\mathbb P(\mathbb C^4)\to S^4$ by
$\pi([v])=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}(v,\jmath v)$. This is independent
of the representative of $[v]$ since $\jmath(cv)=\bar c\,\jmath v$, and
$v,\jmath v$ are linearly independent for $v\ne0$ because $\jmath^2=-1$.
Its fiber over a plane $L$ is $\mathbb P(L)\cong\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$; in
the finite stereographic chart these fibers are the displayed $\ell_z$, and
the remaining fiber is $\ell_\infty$. Write $z_1=x^0+ix^1$ and
$z_2=x^2+ix^3$, orient the finite base chart by
$dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and orient each fiber by its
complex orientation. These orientations induce the complex orientation of
$\mathbb P^3$ in base-then-fiber order; swapping these factors has sign
$(-1)^{4\cdot2}=+1$, so this also agrees with fiber-then-base order. Let
$u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ be the positive point class. For this positive
twistor orientation, $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$; consequently, if the underlying
topological bundle is $\pi^*E$ for a bundle $E\to S^4$ with $c_1(E)=0$, then
$c_2(E)=ku$.

Let $A$ be a framed unitary ASD connection on the round oriented $S^4$, let $\mathcal E$ be its Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$, and let $k=-q_N(A)$. Use the exact coupled cohomology-vanishing input stated below for both $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E^\vee$. Assume also the exact projective GAGA and line-family base-change inputs needed to regard $\mathcal E$ as an algebraic bundle, to make its restrictions trivial on a complex-open neighbourhood of at least one real twistor line, and to apply the diagonal resolution. Finally, use the Chern-character normalization $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$ in $A^*(\mathbb CP^3)_\mathbb Q$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; this normalization is conditional on the twistor pullback class convention matching the framed charge.

Under these inputs,

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

There is a canonical Beilinson three-term monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

whose middle cohomology is $\mathcal E$ and whose terms are

$$U=H^2(Z,\mathcal E(-3)),\qquad K=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2),\qquad U'=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1)),$$

with $\dim U=\dim U'=k$ and $\dim K=2k+N$. The construction is natural in framed bundle isomorphisms and unique up to changes of bases in $U,K,U'$. The values of all global parallel sections form its maximal trivial flat parallel summand, and the connection splits orthogonally into that summand and a summand with no nonzero parallel sections; arbitrary nonflat parallel summands are permitted. The monad construction is additive across this splitting and uses no hypothesis $H^0(Z,\mathcal E)=0$.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and equip $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with the standard Hermitian inner products $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j\overline{u_j}v_j$, which are conjugate-linear in the first variable. For a linear map $T:E\to F$ between these spaces, its Hermitian adjoint $T^\dagger:F\to E$ is characterized by $\langle Tu,v\rangle_F=\langle u,T^\dagger v\rangle_E$; in the standard bases its matrix is the conjugate transpose. For $A,B\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, define their commutator by $[A,B]:=AB-BA$. Let

$$\mathscr D_{k,N}=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W),\qquad \operatorname{Herm}(V)=\{H\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V):H^\dagger=H\}.$$

Here $\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ is regarded as a real vector space. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)\in\mathscr D_{k,N}$. The complex and real moment maps are the maps $\mu_{\mathbb C}:\mathscr D_{k,N}\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ and $\mu_{\mathbb R}:\mathscr D_{k,N}\to\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ defined by

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ in the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$. Write $Z=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$, fix the right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$, and define $\pi:Z\to S^4$ by $\pi([v])=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}(v,jv)$. Its fibers are the real twistor lines. The complex orientation on $Z$ is the one for which vertical complex orientation followed by the displayed base orientation is the complex orientation. Let $\mathcal O_Z(1)$ be the dual of the tautological line bundle and set $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))\in H^2(Z;\mathbb Z)$, viewed in rational cohomology for $\operatorname{ch}$. Let $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ satisfy $\langle u,[S^4]\rangle=1$.

Fix integers $k\ge0$ and $N\ge2$. Let $E\to S^4$ be a framed Hermitian rank-$N$ bundle, with a smooth unitary connection $A$ and Ward bundle $\mathcal E$ whose underlying smooth bundle is $\pi^*E$. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature and $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$, where $*_g$ is the Hodge star for the stated metric and orientation; assume $F_A^+=0$. Define

$$q_N(E,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

Suppose $\mathcal E$ is the middle cohomology of a holomorphic complex exact at its end terms,

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)^{\oplus k}.$$

Assume this middle cohomology is locally free. Then $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$, $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$, and $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$. For the stated positive twistor orientation,

$$\pi^*u=H^2.$$

Consequently $k=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-q_N(E,A)$.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ bundle, $N\ge2$, with a smooth unitary connection $A$ and a unitary framing $\Phi:E_\infty\to\mathbb C^N$. Its curvature $F_A$ is an anti-Hermitian endomorphism-valued two-form; set $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$, where $*_g$ is the Hodge star for the stated metric and orientation, and assume $F_A^+=0$. The determinant-line connection is the connection induced by $A$ on $\det E=\Lambda^N E$. Its framing at $\infty$ determines a unit vector in $(\det E)_\infty$. With

$$q_N(E,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$$

and determinant Chern-form convention $c(A)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$, one has

$$q_N(E,A)=-\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle\in-\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.$$

Thus $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$ is a nonnegative integer, with the sign corresponding to the anti-self-dual equation $F_A^+=0$.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff
second-countable smooth manifold, possibly with boundary or empty, and let
$\rho_M:H^*(M;\mathbb Z)\to H^*(M;\mathbb R)$ be induced by
$\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$. Write $J_M$ for the natural de Rham
isomorphism from real de Rham cohomology to singular cohomology with real
coefficients.

For every finite-rank smooth complex bundle $E\to M$ with a Hermitian metric
and Hermitian connection $\nabla$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([c_j(\nabla)])=\rho_M(c_j(E)).$$
For every finite-rank smooth real bundle $V\to M$ with any real connection
$D$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([p_j(D)])=\rho_M(p_j(V)).$$
For every oriented Euclidean bundle $W\to M$ of even rank with a
metric-compatible connection $\nabla$, and its Thom-normalized Euler class,
$$J_M([e(\nabla)])=\rho_M(e(W)).$$
Here $c_j(\nabla)$, $p_j(D)$, and $e(\nabla)$ use the normalizations in
[[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], while $c_j(E)$,
$p_j(V)$, and $e(W)$ are the published topological classes. In particular
$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line and
$p_j(V)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(V_{\mathbb C})$. These are equalities after passage to
real coefficients; no equality with integral torsion is asserted.

Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, with their standard Hermitian products. Let $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Define the raw moment maps

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J,$$

and assume $\mu_{\mathbb C}=0$. Put $K=V\oplus V\oplus W$. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$ put

$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\dagger+\bar z_2,B_1^\dagger-\bar z_1,I^\dagger)^T,\qquad D_z=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger\\a_z^\dagger\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then

$$D_zD_z^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger b_z&\mu_{\mathbb C}\\\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger&a_z^\dagger a_z\end{pmatrix},\qquad b_z^\dagger b_z-a_z^\dagger a_z=\mu_{\mathbb R}.$$

The maps $b_z^\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and

$$P_z=1-D_z^\dagger\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$

is the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\mathbb R^4$. The projection connection $\nabla=P\,d$ is unitary and satisfies $F^+=0$ for the positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$.

In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ on $\mathbb P^3$, put $A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1$, $C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2$ and

$$\alpha=(A,C,J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,\qquad\beta=(-C,A,I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2).$$

The polynomial identity is $\beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C}+\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R}-\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger$. With $\sigma(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$, one has $\beta(v)=\alpha(\sigma v)^\dagger$. The real line over $z$ is $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively. It preserves the framing representation $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$.

This proves a forward raw block construction. It does not assert that every real Ward monad has this normal form, that its inverse extraction is unique, or that the connection extends with charge $k$; those global correspondence and charge assertions require their separate proofs.

derivations.claim: The entrywise-conjugation counterexample remains valid for the literal source equations; it is not a defect in the raw block supplied by [F5]. The source's displayed M also ends its first block row with P* despite declaring P of size k×N, so that entry has N rows rather than k in general. These displays cannot be substituted for an intrinsic real normal-form proof. Use exactly [A1]'s intrinsic existence and uniqueness conclusions.

The reconstructed monad in [F1] is linear with locally free middle bundle, trivial on every real line, and has the positive Hermitian Ward pairing and unitary framing fixed in the definition. Its dimensions are those required by [A1]. Thus, assuming the exact supplier [A1], extract the raw tuple from its intrinsic normal form. Its monad composition vanishes, so [F5]'s polynomial identity makes both raw moment coefficients zero. Full fiber rank on each real line and [F5]'s Gram/rank equivalence identify the locus exactly with stable-and-costable regularity. Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, standard Hermitian $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ and ADHM data $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with the complex equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Stability means that the $B_1,B_2$ words applied to $I(W)$ span $V$; costability means no nonzero common invariant subspace of $V$ lies in $\ker J$; regular means both. Set

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

For every $\zeta>0$, each stable $GL(V)$ orbit meets $\mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V$ in exactly one $U(V)$ orbit, and the inclusion induces a diffeomorphism of smooth real manifolds

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^s/GL(V).$$

At $\zeta=0$, every stable datum satisfying the real equation is automatically costable. Each regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one unitary orbit, giving instead

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=0,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V).$$

Both identifications are equivariant for the compact rotation/framing torus in the raw-data convention. For $k=0$ all spaces are points. This theorem identifies the stated finite-dimensional quotients; it asserts no correspondence with sheaves or ASD connections, and no identification of the entire positive-FI quotient with the zero-FI regular locus.

Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and be stable, meaning that the vectors obtained by applying all words in $B_1,B_2$ to $I(W)$ span $V$. Costable means that no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$, and regular means stable and costable. On $\mathbb P^2$ with coordinates $[z_0:z_1:z_2]$, define

$$\alpha=\begin{pmatrix}z_0B_1-z_1\\z_0B_2-z_2\\z_0J\end{pmatrix}:V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O,\qquad \beta=\begin{pmatrix}-z_0B_2+z_2&z_0B_1-z_1&z_0I\end{pmatrix}:(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O\to V\otimes\mathcal O(1).$$

Then $\beta\alpha=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$, $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map, and $\beta$ is surjective at every point. The three-term complex is a monad, meaning it is exact at its first and last terms; its middle cohomology $\mathcal E=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is torsion-free of rank $N$, has Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and has a canonical framing $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. Every framed torsion-free sheaf with this rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial arises uniquely up to simultaneous change of basis in $V$ from this construction. For a finite-type complex scheme $S$, a family of ADHM data consists of a rank-$k$ vector bundle $\mathcal V$ on $S$, the fixed framing bundle $\mathcal W=W\otimes\mathcal O_S$, endomorphisms $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal V)$, and maps $I:\mathcal W\to\mathcal V$, $J:\mathcal V\to\mathcal W$ satisfying $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ as a section of $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal V)\otimes\mathcal O_S$ and stable on every geometric fiber. Isomorphisms of such data are vector-bundle isomorphisms of $\mathcal V$ intertwining $B_i,I,J$ and acting identically on $\mathcal W$. A framed sheaf family consists of a coherent sheaf $\mathcal E$ on $\mathbb P^2\times S$ flat over $S$, together with a relative framing $\Phi:\mathcal E|_{L_\infty\times S}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty\times S}$; its closed fibers are required to be torsion-free of rank $N$ with the Hilbert polynomial in the Statement. Isomorphisms of framed sheaf families commute with $\Phi$. If the relative cohomology bundles and the canonical base-change maps satisfy the ranks and isomorphism hypotheses of the preceding Beilinson lemma, the monad construction and its inverse are inverse on isomorphism classes of these families, and the monad middle cohomology is flat over $S$.

For a fixed ADHM datum $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ and its framed sheaf $(\mathcal E,\phi)$, let $D=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. A first-order framed ADHM deformation is a family over $D$ with a specified identification of its special fiber with $x$, modulo isomorphisms that induce the identity under this identification and on $W$. A first-order framed sheaf deformation is a framed sheaf family over $D$ as defined above, with a specified special-fiber isomorphism $\theta:\mathcal E_D|_{\mathbb P^2\times\{0\}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal E$ satisfying $\Phi|_{L_\infty\times\{0\}}=\phi\circ\theta|_{L_\infty}$; its isomorphisms commute with $\Phi$ and induce the identity under $\theta$. Every first-order framed-sheaf family over $D$ satisfies the relative cohomology-bundle and base-change hypotheses of the preceding Beilinson lemma, as proved in step 5.1. Consequently, the first-order correspondence gives inverse maps on all the identified-special-fiber deformation classes defined here and on their tangent vector spaces. Explicitly, define $d_1:\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ by

$$d_1(\dot B_1,\dot B_2,\dot I,\dot J)=[\dot B_1,B_2]+[B_1,\dot B_2]+\dot I J+I\dot J,$$

and define $d_0:\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W)$ by $d_0(\xi)=([\xi,B_1],[\xi,B_2],\xi I,-J\xi)$. A direct expansion of the ADHM equation gives $d_1\circ d_0=0$. The ADHM first-order tangent vector space is $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$. Within the stated family range, the first-order correspondence identifies the corresponding ADHM tangent classes with the tangent vector space of the framed-sheaf deformation classes just specified. The sheaf is locally free exactly when the ADHM datum is costable; hence the regular locus is the locally-free sheaf locus. Combined with the real/complex quotient theorem, positive-FI data correspond to all such framed torsion-free sheaves, while the zero-FI real quotient corresponds to the locally-free locus. The framing representation has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a^{-1}$ and the dual framing has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a$.

Let $n\in\{2,3\}$, $X=\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$, $X^{an}$ its complex analytic space, and $\eta:X^{an}\to X$ the canonical morphism of ringed spaces. Let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ denote the abelian category of all sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules on a ringed space $Y$, and let $D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y))$ be the category of bounded-below cochain complexes in it with quasi-isomorphisms inverted; use the cochain shift convention $K[q]^m=K^{m+q}$ with differential $(-1)^q d_K$. For coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ placed in degree zero, define the global derived morphism groups

$$\operatorname{Ext}^q_Y(\mathcal F,\mathcal G):=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y))}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G[q]),\qquad q\ge0.$$

On $X$, these groups can be computed from a bounded cochain complex $P^\bullet$ of finite-rank locally free sheaves together with a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to\mathcal F$, by $H^q(R\Gamma(X,\mathcal H om^\bullet(P^\bullet,\mathcal G)))$; the analogous computation applies to the analytified resolution on $X^{an}$.

Define analytification by $\operatorname{An}_X(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F^{an}:=\eta^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{\eta^{-1}\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_{X^{an}}$. It is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence from coherent algebraic $\mathcal O_X$-modules (locally finitely presented modules) to coherent analytic $\mathcal O_{X^{an}}$-modules (locally finitely presented modules). For every coherent $\mathcal F$, the canonical cohomology comparison

$$\gamma^q_{\mathcal F}:H^q(X,\mathcal F)=R^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q(X^{an},\mathcal F^{an})=R^q\Gamma(X^{an},\mathcal F^{an})$$

is an isomorphism for all $q\ge0$. For coherent $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$, the map

$$\epsilon^q_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}:\operatorname{Ext}^q_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}^q_{X^{an}}(\mathcal F^{an},\mathcal G^{an})$$

is the map obtained by analytifying a finite locally free resolution of $\mathcal F$ and applying the cohomology comparisons term by term; independence of the chosen resolution makes it canonical. It is an isomorphism for all $q\ge0$, and for $q=0$ it is the usual comparison of algebraic and holomorphic morphisms. Here $H^q$ is sheaf cohomology computed by right-derived global sections using a supplied functorial injective-resolution datum.

Let $i:L_\infty\hookrightarrow X$ be the fixed hyperplane inclusion, where $L_\infty=\{z_0=0\}$, and let $i^{an}:L_\infty^{an}\hookrightarrow X^{an}$ be its analytification. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module, $i^*\mathcal F:=\mathcal O_{L_\infty}\otimes_{i^{-1}\mathcal O_X}i^{-1}\mathcal F$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $(i^*\mathcal F)^{an}\cong(i^{an})^*(\mathcal F^{an})$, so restriction to the fixed hyperplane commutes with analytification.

For the family clause, let $S$ be a finite-type complex scheme, put $Y=X\times S$, and let $p:Y\to S$ be projection. Write $\eta_S:S^{an}\to S$ and $\eta_Y:Y^{an}\to Y$ for analytification; then $Y^{an}\cong X^{an}\times S^{an}$, with analytic projection $p^{an}:Y^{an}\to S^{an}$. Let $\mathcal E$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module flat over $S$, meaning that for every $y\in Y$ the stalk $\mathcal E_y$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,p(y)}$. For each closed point $s\in S$ with residue field $\kappa(s)=\mathbb C$, let $j_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ be its inclusion, $X_s:=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, $i_s:X_s\hookrightarrow Y$, $p_s:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ the projection, and $\mathcal E_s:=i_s^*\mathcal E$. Let $t\in S^{an}$ be the corresponding analytic point, with inclusion $j_t:\{t\}\to S^{an}$, fiber $X_t^{an}:=Y^{an}\times_{S^{an}}\{t\}$, inclusion $i_t^{an}:X_t^{an}\hookrightarrow Y^{an}$, projection $p_t^{an}:X_t^{an}\to\{t\}$, and $\mathcal E_t^{an}:=(i_t^{an})^*\mathcal E^{an}$. For a morphism $f$ of ringed spaces, write $R^qf_*$ for the $q$th cohomology sheaf of the derived direct image computed from a supplied functorial injective resolution; on an open $V$ of the target, $(f_*I)(V)=I(f^{-1}V)$. The canonical algebraic base-change map

$$\beta^{alg}_{q,s}:(R^qp_*\mathcal E)\otimes_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s)\longrightarrow H^q(X_s,\mathcal E_s)$$

is the cohomology-and-base-change map induced by the derived base-change morphism $Lj_s^*Rp_*\mathcal E\to R(p_s)_*Li_s^*\mathcal E$, where $L(-)^*$ is the left-derived pullback functor, after the canonical edge identification $(R^qp_*\mathcal E)\otimes\kappa(s)\cong H^q(Lj_s^*Rp_*\mathcal E)$ when the direct-image cohomology sheaves in the relevant degrees are locally free. Define $\beta^{an}_{q,t}:(R^qp^{an}_*\mathcal E^{an})\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S^{an}}}\kappa(t)\to H^q(X_t^{an},\mathcal E_t^{an})$ by the analogous analytic derived base-change morphism and edge identification. Define the canonical comparison

$$c_q:(R^qp_*\mathcal E)^{an}\longrightarrow R^qp^{an}_*\mathcal E^{an}$$

by the following construction. For every algebraic open $V\subseteq S$, the morphism $\eta_Y^{-1}\mathcal E\to\mathcal E^{an}$ and the natural pullback map on sheaf cohomology give a map $H^q(p^{-1}V,\mathcal E)\to H^q((p^{an})^{-1}(\eta_S^{-1}V),\mathcal E^{an})$. These maps are compatible with restriction, so they induce a morphism from the sheafification of the first cohomology presheaf, identified with $R^qp_*\mathcal E$, to $\eta_{S*}R^qp^{an}_*\mathcal E^{an}$. The adjoint of this morphism under $\eta_S^{-1}(-)\otimes_{\eta_S^{-1}\mathcal O_S}\mathcal O_{S^{an}}\dashv\eta_{S*}$ is $c_q$. Whenever the direct-image cohomology sheaves are locally free of finite rank and both base-change maps $\beta^{alg}_{q,s}$ and $\beta^{an}_{q,t}$ are isomorphisms for every such $s$ and its corresponding $t$, $c_q$ is an isomorphism; on each fiber its induced map commutes with the two base-change maps and the absolute cohomology comparison $\gamma^q_{\mathcal E_s}$. No assertion is made that an arbitrary holomorphic family over a nonproper algebraic base algebraizes.

Assume full AC and the following exact projective GAGA comparison: analytification on $\mathbb P^3_{\mathbb C}$ is an exact tensor equivalence on coherent sheaves and induces cohomology isomorphisms. The local smooth integrable-Dolbeault frame theorem is supplied by the explicit local proof below, rather than assumed as a new analytic input.

For integers $k\ge0$, $N\ge2$, let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$. A framed ASD object is a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ bundle $E\to S^4$, a smooth unitary connection $A$, a unitary framing at infinity, $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$, and $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)=-k$, modulo unitary bundle isomorphisms preserving the connection and framing; write $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ for this set.

Set $Z=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$, let $j$ be the fixed right quaternionic structure with $j^2=-1$, and define $\sigma([v])=[jv]$ and $\pi([v])=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}(v,jv)\in\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$. For $x\in S^4$, the real twistor line is $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $L_\infty$ is the fiber over infinity. A positive Hermitian Ward reality datum on a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle $\mathcal E\to Z$ is a nondegenerate holomorphic pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$ and such that

$$h_x(s,t)=b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$$

is independent of $z\in L_x$ and positive definite on $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$. A unitary framing on $L_\infty$ is an isomorphism $\Phi:\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{L_\infty}^{\oplus N}$ that is unitary for the form induced by $b$. Let $\mathcal O_Z(1)$ be the dual tautological line bundle, put $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$, and require $\mathcal E|_{L_x}\cong\mathcal O_{L_x}^{\oplus N}$ for every real twistor line and $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$.

Then $\widehat E_x=H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ forms a smooth rank-$N$ Hermitian bundle on $S^4$. For the ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_{L_x}$ of $L_x$, its first infinitesimal neighbourhood is the closed subscheme with structure sheaf $\mathcal O_Z/\mathcal I_{L_x}^2$. Extend each section of $\widehat E_x$ holomorphically and uniquely to that neighbourhood and differentiate the extension in the family of lines; this defines the Ward connection $\widehat\nabla$. The form induced by $b$ is smooth and is preserved by $\widehat\nabla$; this is a conclusion, not an independent metric-compatibility assumption.

Use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ with rank-two complex spinor bundles $S^+$ and $S^-$, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. A point of $L_x=\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is a complex line $\ell\subset S_x^+$, and $\ell\otimes S_x^-$ is the corresponding complex alpha-plane. Under these hypotheses, the Ward construction gives a bijection between the framed ASD classes in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ and isomorphism classes of the specified framed Ward data, where Ward isomorphisms preserve the holomorphic bundle, pairing $b$, and framing $\Phi$. The reconstructed Ward connection satisfies $F^+=0$ and $q_N=-k$. The inverse sends a framed ASD connection to the holomorphic structure on $\pi^*E$ whose vertical part is the standard Dolbeault operator and whose horizontal $(0,1)$ part is induced by $A$ along the horizontal lifts of vectors in these alpha-planes, using the Levi-Civita horizontal distribution of $\pi$. Define $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$, with $S^1=\{u\in\mathbb C:|u|=1\}$, $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N\in S^1$, and $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. It acts on $S^4$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$, on framed ASD classes by inverse pullback and postcomposition of the framing by $h$, and on $Z$ by $g([\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2])=[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$; the induced action on framed Ward data is inverse pullback by $g$ together with postcomposition of $\Phi$ by $h$. Both maps preserve the framing, Hermitian form, charge, and these torus actions. Reducible bundles and flat summands are included; no irreducibility assumption is imposed.

Let $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, and equip $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian products. Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ and $Z=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$ have the twistor projection $\pi([v])=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}(v,jv)$ and antiholomorphic involution $\sigma([v])=[jv]$ specified in the preceding twistor definition, with $j^2=-1$. Let $E\to S^4$ be a framed Hermitian bundle with a smooth unitary connection $A$, unitary framing at infinity, and $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$ for the unit round metric and positive orientation specified in the twistor definition. Define $q_N(E,A)=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$. Let $\mathcal E$ be its holomorphic Ward bundle, with underlying smooth bundle $\pi^*E$. A framed positive Ward bundle includes a nondegenerate holomorphic pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$, whose induced form $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is positive on $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ for every real twistor line $L_x$, and a unitary framing on the infinity line $L_\infty$.

Assume its monad is the holomorphic complex

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal O_Z\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

with $\beta\alpha=0$, locally split injective and surjective end maps, locally free middle cohomology $\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$, and $\dim_\mathbb C U=\dim_\mathbb C U'=k$, $\dim_\mathbb C S=2k+N$. Then the real monad is equivalent to a raw datum $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ on $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ in exactly the convention

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0.$$

The tuple is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$, costable when no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$, and regular when both hold. Equivalently, the raw block map

$$D_z=\begin{pmatrix}-B_2+z_2&B_1-z_1&I\\ B_1^\dagger-\bar z_1&B_2^\dagger-\bar z_2&J^\dagger\end{pmatrix}:V\oplus V\oplus W\to V\oplus V$$

is onto for every $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$. Its kernel projection connection on the finite stereographic chart is $\nabla=P\,d$, where $P$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\ker D_z$; it extends over infinity, has the specified framing, and equals the Ward connection. Changes of normalized monad bases, meaning chain isomorphisms preserving the lifted pairing and infinity framing, induce exactly the simultaneous $U(k)$ action on raw data, and inverse matrix extraction recovers the same $U(k)$ orbit. With $q_N(E,A)=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$ for the framed ASD connection $A$, the resulting charge is $k=-q_N(E,A)=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$. The entrywise conjugation candidate is refuted by the recorded comparison lemma and is not used in the intrinsic real monad normalization.

Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian products, and let $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $P:W\to V$, and $Q:V\to W$. Identify the conjugate spaces with these standard-coordinate spaces, so the bars below mean entrywise complex conjugation. Suppose the source-convention equations are

$$[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]+PQ=0,\qquad [\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]-PP^\dagger+Q^\dagger Q=0.$$

For $B_i=\overline{\alpha_i}$, $I=\overline P$, and $J=\overline Q$, use the raw moment maps

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

Under this proposed substitution,

$$B_i=\overline{\alpha_i},\qquad I=\overline P,\qquad J=\overline Q,$$

the raw complex moment map vanishes, but the raw real moment map is

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}=\overline C+\overline X-\overline Y,$$

where $C=[\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]$, $X=PP^\dagger$, and $Y=Q^\dagger Q$. The conjugated source real equation gives $\overline C-\overline X+\overline Y=0$, so on source solutions the proposed raw real moment map equals $2\overline C$; the source equations alone therefore do not establish its vanishing. This failure occurs for the explicit $k=N=2$ solution of the two displayed source equations in the proof below; no source full-rank condition is asserted for that witness.

Assume full AC. Let $k\ge0$ and
$N\ge2$. On $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ with homogeneous coordinates
$(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$, set
$$j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2) =(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1), \qquad \sigma([z])=[jz].$$
For each $(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$, let $\ell_z$ be the real twistor line

$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,$$
and let $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Suppose
$$\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha} \mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta} \mathcal O(1)\otimes U'$$
is a complex of holomorphic vector bundles with $\beta\alpha=0$, locally split
injective and surjective end maps, and locally free middle cohomology
$F=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ of rank $N$, where
$\dim_\mathbb C U=\dim_\mathbb C U'=k$ and
$\dim_\mathbb C S=2k+N$. Suppose $F|_{\ell_z}$ is holomorphically trivial for
every $z$, and it has a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian pairing
$h_F:F\to D(F)$ fixed by the canonical double-dual identification, where
$D(F)=(\sigma^*\overline F)^\vee$. For a $\sigma$-invariant real line $\ell$
and sections $s,t\in H^0(\ell,F|_\ell)$, the induced first-slot-linear
Hermitian form is the constant value of
$x\mapsto h_{F,x}(s(x))(\overline{t(\sigma x)})$; assume it is positive
definite. This is the line-form convention of the preceding first-order
real-structure definition. At the monad level, for a homogeneous linear

differentials $-\beta^\#$ and $\alpha^\#$, so its cohomology is $D(F)$ and

Suppose also that a
unitary framing identifies $F|_{\ell_\infty}$ isometrically with
