Then there are Hermitian
spaces $V$ and $W$ of dimensions $k$ and $N$, with $W$ carrying the prescribed
framing, and maps
$$B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V),\qquad I:W\to V,\qquad J:V\to W$$
such that, after a pairing-preserving framed chain identification, the monad
maps are
$$\alpha= \begin{pmatrix} A\\ C\\ J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \beta=(-C,\ A,\ I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2),$$
where
$$A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1,\qquad C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2.$$
The extracted maps satisfy both zero-moment equations
$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0.$$
They are stable, meaning the vectors
$B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$, and costable, meaning no nonzero
subspace invariant under both $B_i$ is contained in $\ker J$. Conversely,
every such regular datum with both moments zero gives a locally split monad
with the stated real-line positivity and infinity framing.
Here $\dagger$ denotes adjoint in the indicated Hermitian spaces.

In the next assertion, a normalized framed isomorphism is a chain
isomorphism preserving the lifted pairing and the specified infinity frame.
Such isomorphisms correspond exactly to the simultaneous $U(V)$ action
$$(B_1,B_2,I,J)\longmapsto (gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1}),\qquad g\in U(V).$$
Thus inverse coefficient extraction recovers precisely one $U(V)$ orbit; when
$k=0$, $U(0)$ is trivial, and every constant flat summand is retained as an
unused orthogonal subspace of $W$.

For $t_1,t_2\in U(1)$, choose an orthonormal framed basis
$w_1,\ldots,w_N$ of $W$ and phases $e_1,\ldots,e_N\in U(1)$, and let
$h(w_a)=e_a^{-1}w_a$. The coordinate action
$(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto
(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ acts on data by
$$(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto (t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ).$$
The corresponding chain factors on the source, middle and target terms are,
respectively,
$(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$, and $1$.

The same extraction and classification hold naturally for first-order
families over $A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with
$\bar\epsilon=\epsilon$ in the following exact locally-free/base-change
range: the three modules are free of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, the end maps are
locally split, the middle cohomology is locally free and commutes with
reduction, its global section module is free and commutes with reduction, the
coefficient-image submodule in the middle term is a direct summand and
commutes with reduction, and each fixed real-line restriction is trivial
with its section module commuting with reduction. The framing and pairing
are defined over $A$, while positivity is required only on the reduced
complex; adjoints on these modules use the coefficient involution and the
induced $A$-Hermitian forms. Call an $A$-valued datum regular when its
reduction is stable and costable. The extracted matrices lie over $A$ and
obey the same moment equations. Conversely, every $A$-valued regular datum
whose raw
monad satisfies these same global-section, coefficient-image and real-line
base-change conditions gives a family in this range. Pairing-preserving
framed family isomorphisms correspond exactly to
$U(k,A)=\{g:g^\dagger g=1\}$. This assertion is restricted to reduction and
the involution-preserving base maps $\epsilon\mapsto r\epsilon$ with
$r\in\mathbb R$.

For the finite algebraic monad resolution, let
$H_{\rm alg}=c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ and
$H_{\rm top}=c_1^{\rm top}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$. The hyperplane cycle
map identifies these classes in their respective theories. Then
$\operatorname{ch}(F)=N-kH_{\rm alg}^2$ and
$c_2^{\rm alg}(F)=kH_{\rm alg}^2$. Its topological line class is the same
$H_{\rm top}$ and $c_2^{\rm top}(F)=kH_{\rm top}^2$. Define
$\jmath:\mathbb C^4\to\mathbb C^4$ by
$\jmath(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$,
so $\jmath^2=-1$. Identify $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ with the set of
$\jmath$-invariant complex two-planes in $\mathbb C^4$, and define the twistor
quotient map $\pi:\mathbb P(\mathbb C^4)\to S^4$ by
$\pi([v])=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}(v,\jmath v)$. This is independent
of the representative of $[v]$ since $\jmath(cv)=\bar c\,\jmath v$, and
$v,\jmath v$ are linearly independent for $v\ne0$ because $\jmath^2=-1$.
Its fiber over a plane $L$ is $\mathbb P(L)\cong\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$; in
the finite stereographic chart these fibers are the displayed $\ell_z$, and
the remaining fiber is $\ell_\infty$. Write $z_1=x^0+ix^1$ and
$z_2=x^2+ix^3$, orient the finite base chart by
$dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and orient each fiber by its
complex orientation. These orientations induce the complex orientation of
$\mathbb P^3$ in base-then-fiber order; swapping these factors has sign
$(-1)^{4\cdot2}=+1$, so this also agrees with fiber-then-base order. Let
$u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ be the positive point class. For this positive
twistor orientation, $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$; consequently, if the underlying
topological bundle is $\pi^*E$ for a bundle $E\to S^4$ with $c_1(E)=0$, then
$c_2(E)=ku$.

Let $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ carry the antiholomorphic coordinate involution $\sigma([\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2])=[-\bar\lambda_2:\bar\lambda_1:-\bar\mu_2:\bar\mu_1]$. A linear monad is a locally split exact complex at its ends
$$
\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal O(1)\otimes U'
$$
with locally free middle cohomology $F=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$, where $U,S,U'$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces. Write all coefficient matrices in fixed bases, with $P^\dagger=\overline P^T$. For a degree-one matrix $P(z)$ put $P^\#(z)=P(jz)^\dagger$ and define the signed dual monad $D(M):(\overline{U'})^\vee\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\xrightarrow{-\beta^\#}(\overline S)^\vee\otimes\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\alpha^\#}(\overline U)^\vee\otimes\mathcal O(1)$; its cohomology identifies with $D(F):=(\sigma^*\overline F)^\vee$, the holomorphic dual of the pullback of the conjugate bundle, and dualizing twice uses $(P^\#)^\#=-P$ and $D^2(M)=M$. By a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian self-pairing we mean an isomorphism $h_F:F\to D(F)$ that is linear in its first variable, conjugate-linear in its second, and fixed by this bidual operation. Assume $H^0(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$, $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ for every $q\ge0$, and $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-2))=0$ for $q=0,1,2$. For any two such monads, every holomorphic morphism of their middle cohomology bundles lifts to a unique constant chain map between the monads. In particular, for a monad with a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian self-pairing, the unique lift is a chain isomorphism with Hermitian middle map $H=H^\dagger$ and normalized identities
$$
\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H,\qquad \beta(jz)^\dagger=-H\alpha(z),
$$
where $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$ and the end spaces are identified by the lifted pairing.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and equip $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with the standard Hermitian inner products $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j\overline{u_j}v_j$, which are conjugate-linear in the first variable. For a linear map $T:E\to F$ between these spaces, its Hermitian adjoint $T^\dagger:F\to E$ is characterized by $\langle Tu,v\rangle_F=\langle u,T^\dagger v\rangle_E$; in the standard bases its matrix is the conjugate transpose. For $A,B\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, define their commutator by $[A,B]:=AB-BA$. Let

$$\mathscr D_{k,N}=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W),\qquad \operatorname{Herm}(V)=\{H\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V):H^\dagger=H\}.$$

Here $\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ is regarded as a real vector space. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)\in\mathscr D_{k,N}$. The complex and real moment maps are the maps $\mu_{\mathbb C}:\mathscr D_{k,N}\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ and $\mu_{\mathbb R}:\mathscr D_{k,N}\to\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ defined by

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ in the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$. Write $Z=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$, fix the right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$, and define $\pi:Z\to S^4$ by $\pi([v])=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}(v,jv)$. Its fibers are the real twistor lines. The complex orientation on $Z$ is the one for which vertical complex orientation followed by the displayed base orientation is the complex orientation. Let $\mathcal O_Z(1)$ be the dual of the tautological line bundle and set $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))\in H^2(Z;\mathbb Z)$, viewed in rational cohomology for $\operatorname{ch}$. Let $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ satisfy $\langle u,[S^4]\rangle=1$.

Fix integers $k\ge0$ and $N\ge2$. Let $E\to S^4$ be a framed Hermitian rank-$N$ bundle, with a smooth unitary connection $A$ and Ward bundle $\mathcal E$ whose underlying smooth bundle is $\pi^*E$. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature and $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$, where $*_g$ is the Hodge star for the stated metric and orientation; assume $F_A^+=0$. Define

$$q_N(E,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

Suppose $\mathcal E$ is the middle cohomology of a holomorphic complex exact at its end terms,

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)^{\oplus k}.$$

Assume this middle cohomology is locally free. Then $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$, $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$, and $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$. For the stated positive twistor orientation,

$$\pi^*u=H^2.$$

Consequently $k=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-q_N(E,A)$.

Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, with their standard Hermitian products. Let $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Define the raw moment maps

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J,$$

and assume $\mu_{\mathbb C}=0$. Put $K=V\oplus V\oplus W$. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$ put

$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\dagger+\bar z_2,B_1^\dagger-\bar z_1,I^\dagger)^T,\qquad D_z=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger\\a_z^\dagger\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then

$$D_zD_z^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger b_z&\mu_{\mathbb C}\\\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger&a_z^\dagger a_z\end{pmatrix},\qquad b_z^\dagger b_z-a_z^\dagger a_z=\mu_{\mathbb R}.$$

The maps $b_z^\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and

$$P_z=1-D_z^\dagger\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$

is the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\mathbb R^4$. The projection connection $\nabla=P\,d$ is unitary and satisfies $F^+=0$ for the positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$.

In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ on $\mathbb P^3$, put $A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1$, $C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2$ and

$$\alpha=(A,C,J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,\qquad\beta=(-C,A,I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2).$$

The polynomial identity is $\beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C}+\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R}-\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger$. With $\sigma(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$, one has $\beta(v)=\alpha(\sigma v)^\dagger$. The real line over $z$ is $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively. It preserves the framing representation $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$.

This proves a forward raw block construction. It does not assert that every real Ward monad has this normal form, that its inverse extraction is unique, or that the connection extends with charge $k$; those global correspondence and charge assertions require their separate proofs.

Assume AC. Let $E$ be a smooth finite-rank complex vector bundle on a finite-dimensional complex manifold, and let $D''$ be a smooth complex-linear operator from its smooth sections to smooth $E$-valued $(0,1)$-forms satisfying $D''(fs)=\bar\partial f\otimes s+fD''s$. Extend it to bundle-valued forms by the graded Leibniz rule and suppose $(D'')^2=0$. Near every point there is a smooth invertible frame matrix $G$ with $D''G=0$. The changes between these frames are holomorphic, defining a unique holomorphic vector-bundle structure with Dolbeault operator $D''$. A smooth bundle map intertwines two such operators exactly when it is holomorphic for these structures. The construction is local and requires no projective GAGA, coherence or global vanishing theorem.

Assume full AC and DC. Let $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$, let $G=\operatorname{Gr}(2,4)$ be the complex Grassmannian of projective lines in $Z$, and let
$$\mathscr L=\{(g,z)\in G\times Z:z\in g\},\qquad p(g,z)=g,\qquad e(g,z)=z$$
be the universal line family and its projections. Let $\mathcal E\to Z$ be a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle, $N\geq2$, with the positive Ward reality datum from the preceding “Zero-FI regular ADHM and framed twistor data” definition: a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$, linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second, satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $\sigma$ is the fixed antiholomorphic involution on $Z$. For each real line $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$, where $\pi:Z\to S^4$ is the twistor projection fixed in that definition, the pairing defines $h_x(s,t)=b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ on $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$, independent of $z\in L_x$; assume $h_x$ is positive definite and $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is holomorphically trivial. Equip its fibers with the metric transported from $h_x$ by evaluation, as in that definition. Let $L_\infty=\pi^{-1}(\infty)$ and fix a unitary trivialization $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong\mathcal O_{L_\infty}^{\oplus N}$ for this metric. Write $p^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $e^{\mathrm{an}}$ for the induced analytic maps. Identify $S^4$ with its real-line locus in $G$, write $g_x\in G$ for the line parameter corresponding to $x\in S^4$, and put $\mathcal H=(p^{\mathrm{an}})_*(e^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal E$.

Let $\operatorname{ev}:(p^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal H\to(e^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal E$ be the canonical evaluation morphism, which evaluates a family of holomorphic sections at the point of its line.

Then, for every real line $L_x$, the canonical degree-zero analytic base-change map
$$\beta^0_{g_x}:\mathcal H_{g_x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{G^{\mathrm{an}},g_x}}\mathbb C(g_x)\longrightarrow H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$$
is an isomorphism, where $\mathbb C(g_x)=\mathcal O_{G^{\mathrm{an}},g_x}/\mathfrak m_{g_x}\cong\mathbb C$ is the residue field. The restriction $\mathcal H|_{S^4}$ is a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with fibre $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ at $x$, and evaluation identifies its pullback to the real incidence family with $(e^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal E$. More precisely, for every real line there is a complex-open neighbourhood in $G$ on whose entire universal-line family the evaluation morphism is an isomorphism. The framing on $L_\infty$ induces a unitary framing of this bundle at $\infty$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]), inherited from the
Noetherian approximation and the finite-free criterion cited below. Let
$f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of finite presentation
([[def-proper-morphism]], [[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]) with
$S$ an arbitrary scheme, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal
O_X$-module ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]) that is flat over $S$
([[def-flat-and-faithfully-flat-modules-and-ring-maps]]); by [F1] $\mathcal F$
is then finitely presented.

Fix $s\in S$ and an integer $q\ge0$, write $\kappa(s)$ for the residue field
([[def-residue-field-scheme-point]]), put $X_s:=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}
\kappa(s)$ with projection $g_s:X_s\to X$ and $\mathcal F_s:=g_s^*\mathcal F$
([[def-pullback-module-ringed-spaces]]), and let
$$\varphi^q_s:(R^qf_*\mathcal F)(s)\longrightarrow H^q(X_s,\mathcal F_s)$$
be the cohomology and base-change map at $s$
([[def-base-change-map-cohomology]], [[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]]).

**(a)** If $\varphi^q_s$ is surjective, then there is an affine open
neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that for every morphism $h:T\to U$,
with $X_T:=X\times_ST$ and projection $g_T:X_T\to X$
([[def-base-change-morphism-schemes]]), the base-change map
$$h^*\bigl(R^qf_*\mathcal F|_U\bigr)\longrightarrow R^qf_{T*}(g_T^*\mathcal F)$$
of [[def-base-change-map-cohomology]] is an isomorphism of $\mathcal
O_T$-modules.

**(b)** Assume moreover that $\varphi^q_s$ is surjective. Then $R^qf_*\mathcal
F$ is locally free of finite rank in a neighbourhood of $s$
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]) if and only if $\varphi^{q-1}_s$ is
surjective; for $q=0$ the condition on $\varphi^{-1}_s$ is automatic, so
$f_*\mathcal F$ is then finite locally free near $s$.

**(c)** Under the hypothesis of (a), $\varphi^q_s$ itself is an isomorphism.

The empty source $X=\varnothing$, the zero sheaf $\mathcal F=0$, the degrees
$q=0$ and $q>0$ with $X_s=\varnothing$, and an arbitrary (not necessarily
Noetherian) base $S$ are included. No flatness or finite-presentation
hypothesis is imposed on $f$ beyond the stated ones, and no projectivity,
Noetherianness or Krull-dimension hypothesis is imposed on $S$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]), inherited from the
Noetherian approximation and the Noetherian-stage construction cited below.
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper
morphism of finite presentation ([[def-proper-morphism]],
[[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]), and let $\mathcal F$ be a
finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module
([[def-finite-type-finite-presentation-module-sheaf]]) that is flat over $A$,
meaning that for every $x\in X$ the stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is a flat module over
the local ring $A_{f(x)}=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A,f(x)}$
([[def-flat-and-faithfully-flat-modules-and-ring-maps]]).

Then there are an integer $r\ge0$ and a bounded complex $K^\bullet$ of finite
projective $A$-modules, concentrated in degrees $0,\dots,r$ and finite free in
all positive degrees, such that for every $A$-algebra $A'$ and every
$q\in\mathbb Z$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$H^q(K^\bullet\otimes_AA')\;\cong\;H^q(X_{A'},\mathcal F_{A'}),$$
where $X_{A'}:=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A'$ with
projection $p:X_{A'}\to X$ ([[def-base-change-morphism-schemes]]) and
$\mathcal F_{A'}:=p^*\mathcal F$ ([[def-pullback-module-ringed-spaces]]). The
isomorphisms are natural in the $A$-algebra $A'$ and compatible with
composition of $A$-algebra maps.

Locally on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ the complex can be made finite free: there
is an open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by affine opens $V$ such that
$K^\bullet\otimes_A\mathcal O(V)$ is a bounded complex of finite free
$\mathcal O(V)$-modules.

The empty source $X=\varnothing$, the zero sheaf $\mathcal F=0$, the
one-member case $r=0$, the zero ring $A=0$, the base change $A'=0$, the
degrees $q<0$ and $q>r$, and the case where $A$ is already finitely generated
over $\mathbb Z$ are included.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $I \trianglelefteq R$ satisfy $I \subseteq J(R)$, and let $M$ be a finitely generated left $R$-module. If $IM=M$, then $M=0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: By [A1], every regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one $U(k)$ orbit. Thus inclusion of the zero-level regular locus induces the stated diffeomorphic identification with the regular complex quotient. The compact action [F1] commutes with gauge and preserves both zero moments, so the identification is $T$-equivariant.

To construct the forward map from an arbitrary regular zero-moment datum, use [F4]'s global raw monad. Write $F=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ and $K=V\oplus V\oplus W$. The identity $\beta(v)=\alpha(\sigma v)^\dagger$ gives $\ker\beta(v)=(\operatorname{im}\alpha(\sigma v))^\perp$. The standard first-slot-linear Hermitian form on $K$ therefore descends to a pairing between $F_v$ and $F_{\sigma v}$: changing either representative by its $\alpha$-image pairs to zero. The annihilator identities show that the induced pairing is nondegenerate; the Hermitian symmetry follows from that on $K$. Conjugate pullback makes it holomorphic. On a finite real line, [F4]'s Euler decomposition identifies its section space with $\ker D_z$ and the pairing with the restricted positive form; at infinity these are exactly $W$ and its fixed frame. The two locally split monad sequences also split as smooth bundles. Their total Chern classes give $c(F)=((1-H)(1+H))^{-k}$, hence $c_1(F)=0$ and $c_2(F)=kH^2$. Thus every hypothesis of the inverse Ward construction [A4] is met. It produces a smooth global framed unitary ASD connection, and [F2]–[F3] give $q_N=-k$ with the specified orientation and trace.

We now prove the additional Ward bridge over $D=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$; it is not part of [A4]'s ordinary Statement. A first-order ASD object means a locally free rank-$N$ module over $C^\infty_{S^4}\otimes D$, with a nondegenerate $D$-Hermitian form positive on reduction, unitary framing and form-preserving connection $\nabla_D$, with $F_{\nabla_D}^+=0$ coefficientwise. Morphisms are framed unitary $D$-linear connection isomorphisms. Pull back and define the vertical/horizontal operator using [A4]'s incidence. Its square vanishes by the same curvature identity coefficientwise. Viewed over $\mathbb C$, this is an integrable Dolbeault operator on a smooth rank-$2N$ bundle, so [F5] supplies holomorphic frames. Multiplication by $\epsilon$ is an intertwining map, hence holomorphic, with square zero and image equal to kernel of complex rank $N$. At a point choose $N$ holomorphic sections $s_a$ whose $\epsilon s_a$ form a basis of that image. The $2N$ sections $s_a,\epsilon s_a$ remain a complex frame nearby by a nonzero determinant. Thus the $s_a$ are a holomorphic $D$-basis. The pairing is holomorphic by metric compatibility as in [A4], and every real-line restriction is the constant free module of its base fibre. This gives the forward first-order Ward object and preserves its framing.

By [A2], regular complex orbits correspond exactly to locally free framed sheaves on $\mathbb P^2$: stability gives torsion-freeness and costability gives local freeness. At positive level, $k=1$, $B_1=B_2=J=0$ and $II^\dagger=\zeta>0$ satisfy both moment equations and are stable, whereas $V\subset\ker J$ violates costability. Thus the positive-FI quotient includes a non-locally-free point and is not identified here with the ordinary ASD sector. This proves the boundary assertion without using any Ward-family claim.

This Ward connection is the raw projection connection on the finite chart. On the complexified line-parameter chart $X$, let $a_X=\alpha_{\lambda_1}$, $b_X=\alpha_{\lambda_2}$ and $S_X=\ker\beta_{\lambda_1}\cap\ker\beta_{\lambda_2}$. Along the real locus these are $a_z,b_z,\ker D_z$; the complement and invertible Gram persist near each real line. Along a parameter direction $v$ in $\mathscr D=\ker(de)$ at $[\lambda]$, the point of $Z$ is fixed, so differentiating $\beta(\lambda)s=0$ for a section $s(X)\in S_X$ gives $\beta(\lambda)\,ds(v)=0$. At the real locus write the component of $ds(v)$ perpendicular to $\ker D_z$ as $a_z u+b_z w$. Since $\beta(\lambda)=f_z(-\lambda_2,\lambda_1)$ on these two summands, its kernel condition is $-\lambda_2u+\lambda_1w=0$. Hence $(u,w)=(\lambda_1r,\lambda_2r)$ and that component is $\alpha(\lambda)r$, zero in monad cohomology. Evaluation therefore transports the canonical relative derivative to $P_zds(v)$. The cotangent uniqueness in [A4]'s incidence construction identifies the full connection with $P\,d$. The global Ward bundle supplies its smooth extension at infinity.

Conversely let $F_D$ be a holomorphic locally free $D$-bundle in the stated monad range. Its underlying complex bundle $G$ has rank $2N$ and is trivial on every real line; no positive complex form on $G$ is assumed. Here is the needed section-bundle argument without that assumption. Algebraize $G$ by [A3] and form the universal proper flat line family $p:\mathscr L\to\operatorname{Gr}(2,4)$, $e:\mathscr L\to Z$, with its graph charts as in [F5]. The locally free $e^*G$ is base-flat. At a real line its fibre has $H^1=0$ and $H^0=\mathbb C^{2N}$. The degree-one base-change map is therefore surjective. By [F5] it is an isomorphism; finiteness from the projective cohomology complex and Nakayama kill the degree-one stalk near that line. The degree-one local-freeness criterion then makes degree-zero base change surjective, hence an isomorphism with locally free section bundle of rank $2N$. Evaluation is an isomorphism on the real line. Removing the proper image of its determinant-zero locus makes it an isomorphism on an entire neighboring line family. Analytifying evaluation and using that holomorphic functions on a product with $\mathbb P^1$ are constant along its fibres identifies the actual analytic section bundle, exactly as in [F5]. Multiplication by $\epsilon$ commutes with evaluation and has image equal to kernel of rank $N$. The local frame argument of step 1.3 now makes this section bundle free of rank $N$ over $\mathcal O\otimes D$ and evaluation $D$-linear. Restriction to the real locus is a smooth free $D$-bundle.

Conversely, start with a framed ASD connection. By [A4] it has its positive Ward bundle, and the reconstruction supplier produces a monad of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, including flat summands. Apply [A5] to this monad to extract its regular zero-moment orbit. Applying step 1.2 to that orbit returns the original framed Ward bundle; the inverse identity in [A4] returns the original connection. Starting with raw data, the cohomology isomorphism in [A4] followed by the chain lifting and inverse extraction in [A6] returns that same normalized monad up to exactly $U(k)$. Thus both composites on framed classes are identities. This uses [A5] only in its stated ASD-to-data direction.

On the graph-chart universal family, $\mathscr D=\ker(de)$ consists of variations $v$ with $v\lambda=0$. The canonical flat derivative along $\mathscr D$ on $e^*F_D$ transfers by evaluation to the pulled-back section bundle. The restriction of cotangent forms gives $p_*\mathscr D^*\cong\Omega^1_{\operatorname{Gr}(2,4)}$: on each line its kernel is $\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2}$ with $H^0=H^1=0$, and the map is equivalently the restriction of linear covectors on $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb C^2,\mathbb C^2)$ to all planes $v\lambda=0$. These planes span that four-dimensional space; both spaces of covectors have dimension four. The same isomorphism tensored with $D$ therefore pushes the partial derivative to a unique full $D$-connection, with the Leibniz rule. It is flat on every alpha-plane, hence ASD on the real locus by the incidence curvature polynomial. Duals, conjugate pullback, pairing and morphisms commute with evaluation and this unique construction. Consequently it preserves the induced $D$-Hermitian form and unitary framing. Evaluation intertwines the reconstructed vertical/horizontal operator with the original one, and starting from a connection recovers all its alpha-plane derivatives, which determine the full connection. These prove inverse identities on framed $D$-objects and morphisms. All constructions commute with reduction and $\epsilon\mapsto r\epsilon$, $r\in\mathbb R$; this also proves the first-order Ward naturality missing from the ordinary supplier.

The action here is the compact $T$ of [F1]. Since $\bar t_i=t_i^{-1}$ and $h^\dagger=h^{-1}$, [F4]'s chain factors are $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$; the induced map at infinity is $h$. Ward reconstruction and inverse extraction commute with these maps by [A4] and [A6]. Thus the bijection of step 3.1 is $T$-equivariant. No assertion for nonunitary complex-torus parameters is needed.

For precision, a tangent vector at a fixed ordinary framed object is a first-order object with identified reduction, modulo isomorphisms inducing identity on that reduction. On the raw side write $x_D=x+\epsilon\dot x$; the tangent quotient is the real-linear kernel of $(d\mu_{\mathbb C},d\mu_{\mathbb R})_x$ modulo $([\xi,B_1],[\xi,B_2],\xi I,-J\xi)$, $\xi^\dagger=-\xi$, restricted to the stated monad/base-change range. On the ASD side smooth first-order bundle transitions differ from the reduced ones by an additive $\operatorname{End}(E)$ cocycle. A partition of unity [F6] splits it: in common bundle notation, for $c_{ij}+c_{jk}=c_{ik}$, $u_i=\sum_j\rho_jc_{ij}$ gives $u_i-u_j=c_{ij}$. A change $1-\epsilon h_0^{-1}h_1/2$ normalizes a metric $h_0+\epsilon h_1$, and a smooth adjustment near infinity fixes the framing. Thus these tangents are represented by $A+\epsilon a$, $a\in\Omega^1(S^4,\mathfrak u(E))$, with $(d_Aa)^+=0$, modulo $d_A\xi$ for smooth $\xi\in\Gamma(\mathfrak u(E))$ with $\xi(\infty)=0$. Here $\mathfrak u(E)$ is the bundle of skew-Hermitian endomorphisms and $d_A$ is the covariant exterior derivative. Restrict to those Ward objects admitting the exact monad, section, coefficient-image and base-change conditions already imposed in the Statement; nothing asserts them for all infinitesimal ASD objects.

Apply [A6] over $D$ to precisely those monads. Its chain lifting also extends over $D$: the two locally split kernel/image sequences give the same Hom restriction maps, whose kernels and cokernels vanish by the degree-zero, degree-one and degree-two groups of $\mathcal O(-1)$ and $\mathcal O(-2)$. The projective twisting-sheaf calculation in [F5] supplies those vanishings over $D$, and $H^0(\mathcal O)=D$, so the lift is uniquely a constant $D$-linear chain map. Uniqueness makes it preserve the lifted pairing whenever the cohomology map does. The raw construction remains valid because every required inverse matrix has invertible reduction, with $(M_0+\epsilon M_1)^{-1}=M_0^{-1}-\epsilon M_0^{-1}M_1M_0^{-1}$, and its real-line Euler decomposition holds over $D$. Together with steps 1.3, 2.3 and 3.2 and [A3]'s exact comparison this gives inverse maps on the restricted first-order classes. If a holomorphic $D$-object needs algebraization, apply absolute GAGA to its coherent underlying complex bundle and to its holomorphic nilpotent endomorphism; full faithfulness transports the $D$-action and exactness transports kernel and image. Its locally free $D$-structure follows from the same rank-$N$ frame argument, so no general relative algebraization theorem is being assumed. The comparison with framed-sheaf families uses [A2] only with its stipulated relative cohomology ranks and base-change isomorphisms. On fixed reductions all first-order equations, derivatives, changes of bases and gauge actions are real-linear in the $\epsilon$ coefficients; evaluation and the inverse uniquely determined connection respect their sums. The induced inverse tangent maps are therefore real-linear. This proves the stated first-order compatibility in exactly its prescribed range, including $k=0$ and flat summands, and completes every clause.

boundaries.evidence: Statement: k=0 is allowed and V=C^0 gives one empty regular datum modulo the trivial U(0), rather than an empty moduli set. The conditional inverse Ward/monad maps preserve its rank-N flat framed sector; family/tangent conclusions remain within the supplied base-change and normal-form hypotheses, not a claim about arbitrary empty families.
Steps 1.2, 2.2 and 5.1 include k=0: the empty block leaves W, its flat framed projection and the same dual-number constructions.
Statement: N>=2 excludes the framing-rank-one boundary; k=1 is allowed by the raw regular-locus and monad suppliers.
Steps 1.2, 3.1 and 5.1 preserve reducible and flat summands. Step 2.1 checks the positive-FI k=1 noncostable point explicitly.
Statement; steps 1.1 and 2.1: The zero-FI regular quotient is identified with ordinary ASD; positive-FI stable boundary points are not transferred to that open locus.

The Statement and proof Given explicitly assume full AC, which supplies DC and countable choice in the proper cohomology and smooth-splitting inputs. Steps 1.3, 2.3, 3.2, 4.2 and 5.1 prove the Ward family and tangent bridge locally in the original stipulated range.
Steps 1.2 and 2.2 construct a positive global real monad, apply inverse Ward and identify its projection connection; the trace charge is minus k.
Step 3.1 applies Ward and reconstruction to an ASD object, then the stated ASD-to-data extraction; cohomology-chain lifting and U(k) classification prove both inverse identities.

risk_review.notes: Forward raw-monad reality, positivity, Ward reconstruction and charge are proved before inverse extraction is applied. The first-order Ward bridge is proved locally over dual numbers with local integrable frames, fixed-line cohomology and canonical incidence connections, and framed morphisms. Tangent assertions retain the original monad/base-change range; no ordinary-set bijection is promoted to a family theorem.

citations.quote:
Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and equip $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with the standard Hermitian inner products $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j\overline{u_j}v_j$, which are conjugate-linear in the first variable. For a linear map $T:E\to F$ between these spaces, its Hermitian adjoint $T^\dagger:F\to E$ is characterized by $\langle Tu,v\rangle_F=\langle u,T^\dagger v\rangle_E$; in the standard bases its matrix is the conjugate transpose. For $A,B\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, define their commutator by $[A,B]:=AB-BA$. Let

$$\mathscr D_{k,N}=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W),\qquad \operatorname{Herm}(V)=\{H\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V):H^\dagger=H\}.$$

Here $\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ is regarded as a real vector space. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)\in\mathscr D_{k,N}$. The complex and real moment maps are the maps $\mu_{\mathbb C}:\mathscr D_{k,N}\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ and $\mu_{\mathbb R}:\mathscr D_{k,N}\to\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ defined by

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a nonempty, connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. Let $G\subseteq U(V,h)$ be a compact non-Abelian matrix Lie group in its specified global form, let $\pi:P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle in a specified bundle sector (an isomorphism class of smooth principal bundles under isomorphisms over $X$), and let $\omega$ be a supplied smooth principal connection. Let $B:\mathfrak g\times\mathfrak g\to\mathbb R$ be a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form invariant under $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$. For local sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$. If $F_i=\sum_a e_a F_i^a$ in a finite basis of $\mathfrak g$, define $B(F_i\wedge F_i):=\sum_{a,b}B(e_a,e_b)F_i^a\wedge F_i^b$; this expression is independent of the basis. Invariance of $B$ makes the local expressions $\beta_B|_{U_i}:=(8\pi^2)^{-1}B(F_i\wedge F_i)$ restrictions of a global four-form $\beta_B$. The **trace-normalized topological charge** is

$$
q_B(P,\omega):=\int_X\beta_B.
$$

The number $q_B(P,\omega)$ is independent of the supplied connection. For a general compact matrix group and invariant $B$, it is a real characteristic number; no integrality is asserted. In the special case $G=SU(2)$ in its defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$, with $h(v,w)=w^*v$ (linear in $v$ and conjugate-linear in $w$) and $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$, the associated Hermitian bundle $E=P\times_{SU(2)}\mathbb C^2$ has

$$
q_B(P,\omega)=-\langle c_2(E),[X]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,
$$

where $c_2(E)\in H^4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the integral second Chern class and $[X]\in H_4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the orientation fundamental class. This sign is fixed by the library convention $c(E,\nabla)=\det(I-\Omega_\nabla/(2\pi i))$.

The Hodge operator $*_g$ on two-forms is characterized by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$ and acts componentwise on $\mathfrak g$-valued forms. Set $F_i^+=(F_i+*_gF_i)/2$ and $F_i^-=(F_i-*_gF_i)/2$. The self-dual sector consists of connections with $F_i^-=0$, equivalently $F_i=*_gF_i$; the anti-self-dual (ASD) sector consists of connections with $F_i^+=0$, equivalently $F_i=-*_gF_i$. These conditions are independent of the local section.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a nonempty, connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with Riemannian metric $g_X$. Let $G\subseteq U(V,h)$ be a compact non-Abelian matrix Lie group in its specified global form, let $P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle, and let $\omega$ be a supplied smooth principal connection. Let $B$ be a positive-definite, symmetric, $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$-invariant bilinear form on $\mathfrak g$. For any local section $s_i$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$. Invariance of $B$ makes the local four-forms $\beta_B|_{U_i}=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}B(F_i\wedge F_i)$ and $\gamma_B|_{U_i}=B(F_i\wedge *_{g_X}F_i)$ restrictions of global forms. Define $q_B=\int_X\beta_B$. For a real scalar $g>0$, define the Euclidean Yang–Mills functional by

$$
S_B(P,\omega):=\frac{1}{g^2}\int_X\gamma_B,
$$

where the Hodge operator is characterized by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_X}$ and acts componentwise on $\mathfrak g$-valued forms. Then

$$
S_B(P,\omega)\geq \frac{8\pi^2}{g^2}\,|q_B(P,\omega)|.
$$

The statement asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of a connection in any charge sector.

Assume full AC. Let $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$, and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian products. A raw datum is $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its moment maps are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

It is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$; it is costable if no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$; it is regular if both conditions hold. Let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ADHM,reg}}_{k,N}$ be the quotient of the regular zero-moment locus by

$$(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1}),\qquad g\in U(V)$$

The stable complex quotient uses the same formula with $g\in GL(V)$.

Give $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ the unit round metric and positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$. modulo unitary bundle isomorphisms preserving the connection and framing; let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ be the set of these classes.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
For every natural number $n\ge2$, the unit sphere $S^n\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ is simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]).

A connection on a finite-rank smooth vector bundle $E\to M$ is flat if and
only if every point of $M$ has a neighborhood carrying a local frame
$(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ of parallel sections, meaning $\nabla_Xe_a=0$ for every
local vector field $X$ and every $a$.

Let $E\to M$ carry a flat connection, meaning $R^\nabla=0$. For every
$p\in M$ there is a coordinate ball $U$ about $p$ such that, whenever two
piecewise smooth paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to U$ have the same initial
and terminal points,

$$P_{\gamma_0}=P_{\gamma_1}.$$

This is a local assertion; it makes no claim about transport around loops in a
non-simply-connected larger domain.

derivations.claim: When $k=0$, $V=0$. There is exactly one quadruple of maps, all with zero-dimensional domain or codomain. Both moment equations are the unique equality of endomorphisms of $0$; the span of the empty family is $0=V$, and no nonzero subspace of $V$ exists. Thus this datum is stable and costable, and the quotient by $U(0)$ is one point.

The Hodge identity and $*_gF_A=-F_A$ give $\int_{S^4}|F_A|_B^2\,d\mathrm{vol}=\int B(F_A\wedge *_gF_A)=-8\pi^2q_N=0$, where the norm uses the round metric and the positive form [F2]. Its continuous nonnegative integrand must vanish everywhere: a positive value would give a positive integral on an open neighborhood. Hence $F_A=0$. For two piecewise smooth paths from $\infty$ to $x$, their concatenation is a loop and is null-homotopic by [F3]. Pull back a cover by coordinate balls with local parallel frames to the compact homotopy square; a Lebesgue number gives a finite subdivision with each cell mapped into one such ball. Transport along a continuous edge is defined using that ball's parallel frame; on overlaps parallel-frame changes are locally constant, so the definition agrees along each connected edge. Each cell has identity boundary transport. Sweeping through successive cells cancels the transport on shared edges with its inverse and leaves identity transport around the external boundary. Thus transport from $\infty$ is path-independent. Transporting the fixed framed orthonormal basis gives smooth parallel sections, as seen in local parallel frames, and a framed unitary isomorphism with the trivial flat bundle. A parallel unitary automorphism preserving the framing is identity, since its value everywhere is transported from its identity value at $\infty$. Conversely, the trivial framed flat connection is ASD and has $q_N=0$. Thus the sector has exactly one class and its based parallel stabilizer is trivial.

Pairing the unique empty datum with the trivial framed flat bundle gives the bijection of the two singleton sets established in steps 1.1 and 1.2. For the additional comparison, impose all hypotheses [A1], including full AC: the conditional correspondence then applies, and its bijection necessarily sends that datum to this class, with $q_N=0$. The direct classification and its no-stabilizer conclusion were proved before this comparison and require no irreducibility assumption.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and equip $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with the standard Hermitian inner products $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j\overline{u_j}v_j$, which are conjugate-linear in the first variable. For a linear map $T:E\to F$ between these spaces, its Hermitian adjoint $T^\dagger:F\to E$ is characterized by $\langle Tu,v\rangle_F=\langle u,T^\dagger v\rangle_E$; in the standard bases its matrix is the conjugate transpose. For $A,B\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, define their commutator by $[A,B]:=AB-BA$. Let

$$\mathscr D_{k,N}=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W),\qquad \operatorname{Herm}(V)=\{H\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V):H^\dagger=H\}.$$

Here $\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ is regarded as a real vector space. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)\in\mathscr D_{k,N}$. The complex and real moment maps are the maps $\mu_{\mathbb C}:\mathscr D_{k,N}\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ and $\mu_{\mathbb R}:\mathscr D_{k,N}\to\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ defined by

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, standard Hermitian $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ and ADHM data $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with the complex equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Stability means that the $B_1,B_2$ words applied to $I(W)$ span $V$; costability means no nonzero common invariant subspace of $V$ lies in $\ker J$; regular means both. Set

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

For every $\zeta>0$, each stable $GL(V)$ orbit meets $\mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V$ in exactly one $U(V)$ orbit, and the inclusion induces a diffeomorphism of smooth real manifolds

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^s/GL(V).$$

At $\zeta=0$, every stable datum satisfying the real equation is automatically costable. Each regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one unitary orbit, giving instead

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=0,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V).$$

Both identifications are equivariant for the compact rotation/framing torus in the raw-data convention. For $k=0$ all spaces are points. This theorem identifies the stated finite-dimensional quotients; it asserts no correspondence with sheaves or ASD connections, and no identification of the entire positive-FI quotient with the zero-FI regular locus.

Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and be stable, meaning that the vectors obtained by applying all words in $B_1,B_2$ to $I(W)$ span $V$. Costable means that no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$, and regular means stable and costable. On $\mathbb P^2$ with coordinates $[z_0:z_1:z_2]$, define

$$\alpha=\begin{pmatrix}z_0B_1-z_1\\z_0B_2-z_2\\z_0J\end{pmatrix}:V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O,\qquad \beta=\begin{pmatrix}-z_0B_2+z_2&z_0B_1-z_1&z_0I\end{pmatrix}:(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O\to V\otimes\mathcal O(1).$$

Then $\beta\alpha=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$, $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map, and $\beta$ is surjective at every point. The three-term complex is a monad, meaning it is exact at its first and last terms; its middle cohomology $\mathcal E=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is torsion-free of rank $N$, has Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and has a canonical framing $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. Every framed torsion-free sheaf with this rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial arises uniquely up to simultaneous change of basis in $V$ from this construction. For a finite-type complex scheme $S$, a family of ADHM data consists of a rank-$k$ vector bundle $\mathcal V$ on $S$, the fixed framing bundle $\mathcal W=W\otimes\mathcal O_S$, endomorphisms $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal V)$, and maps $I:\mathcal W\to\mathcal V$, $J:\mathcal V\to\mathcal W$ satisfying $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ as a section of $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal V)\otimes\mathcal O_S$ and stable on every geometric fiber. Isomorphisms of such data are vector-bundle isomorphisms of $\mathcal V$ intertwining $B_i,I,J$ and acting identically on $\mathcal W$. A framed sheaf family consists of a coherent sheaf $\mathcal E$ on $\mathbb P^2\times S$ flat over $S$, together with a relative framing $\Phi:\mathcal E|_{L_\infty\times S}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty\times S}$; its closed fibers are required to be torsion-free of rank $N$ with the Hilbert polynomial in the Statement. Isomorphisms of framed sheaf families commute with $\Phi$. If the relative cohomology bundles and the canonical base-change maps satisfy the ranks and isomorphism hypotheses of the preceding Beilinson lemma, the monad construction and its inverse are inverse on isomorphism classes of these families, and the monad middle cohomology is flat over $S$.

For a fixed ADHM datum $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ and its framed sheaf $(\mathcal E,\phi)$, let $D=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. A first-order framed ADHM deformation is a family over $D$ with a specified identification of its special fiber with $x$, modulo isomorphisms that induce the identity under this identification and on $W$. A first-order framed sheaf deformation is a framed sheaf family over $D$ as defined above, with a specified special-fiber isomorphism $\theta:\mathcal E_D|_{\mathbb P^2\times\{0\}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal E$ satisfying $\Phi|_{L_\infty\times\{0\}}=\phi\circ\theta|_{L_\infty}$; its isomorphisms commute with $\Phi$ and induce the identity under $\theta$. Consequently, the first-order correspondence gives inverse maps on all the identified-special-fiber deformation classes defined here and on their tangent vector spaces. Explicitly, define $d_1:\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ by

$$d_1(\dot B_1,\dot B_2,\dot I,\dot J)=[\dot B_1,B_2]+[B_1,\dot B_2]+\dot I J+I\dot J,$$

and define $d_0:\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W)$ by $d_0(\xi)=([\xi,B_1],[\xi,B_2],\xi I,-J\xi)$. A direct expansion of the ADHM equation gives $d_1\circ d_0=0$. The ADHM first-order tangent vector space is $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$. Within the stated family range, the first-order correspondence identifies the corresponding ADHM tangent classes with the tangent vector space of the framed-sheaf deformation classes just specified. The sheaf is locally free exactly when the ADHM datum is costable; hence the regular locus is the locally-free sheaf locus. Combined with the real/complex quotient theorem, positive-FI data correspond to all such framed torsion-free sheaves, while the zero-FI real quotient corresponds to the locally-free locus. The framing representation has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a^{-1}$ and the dual framing has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a$.

derivations.claim: For $V=W=\mathbb C$, both commutators vanish. Thus $\mu_{\mathbb C}=IJ=0$ and $\mu_{\mathbb R}=|I|^2-|J|^2=\zeta$. Since $I\ne0$, the words of length zero applied to $I(W)$ span $V$, so the datum is stable. Since $J=0$, the nonzero subspace $V$ is invariant and contained in $\ker J$, so the datum is not costable; in particular it is not a zero-FI regular datum. By [F2], its positive-FI complex orbit has a representative with $I=1$ after the $GL(1,\mathbb C)$ change of basis $g=\zeta^{-1/2}$.

Substituting that representative in [F3] gives $\alpha=(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T$ and $\beta=(z_2,-z_1,z_0)$. Their product is $-z_2z_1+z_1z_2=0$. The row $\beta$ is surjective at every projective point because its three entries have no common zero, and $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map because it is nonzero away from $p$. Let $K=\ker\beta$. Projection to the third coordinate restricts to a morphism $\gamma:K\to\mathcal O$. On the affine chart $z_0=1$, put $x=z_1$ and $y=z_2$; a vector in $K$ has the form $(u,v,-yu+xv)$, so $\gamma(K)=(x,y)$ and its kernel is generated by $(-x,-y,0)$, the image of $\alpha$. On any chart away from $p$ where $z_1$ or $z_2$ is a unit, the same equations show that $\gamma$ is onto and its kernel is generated by $\alpha$. Hence $K/\operatorname{im}\alpha\cong I_p$ globally, where $I_p$ is the ideal sheaf of $p$.

At $p$, the local ideal $(x,y)$ is not principal: if it were generated by one element in the regular local ring $\mathbb C[x,y]_{(x,y)}$, its quotient by the maximal ideal would have dimension at most one, whereas $(x,y)/(x,y)^2$ has dimension two. Therefore $I_p$ is not locally free at $p$. Its framing on $L_\infty$ is the canonical trivialization because $p\notin L_\infty$. This exhibits a positive-FI stable point outside the costable, locally-free zero-FI locus; the correspondence with ordinary ASD moduli is restricted to that zero-FI locus and does not absorb this boundary point.
